With [[Todd Gilles]], she won four [[ISU Junior Grand Prix]] medals and the [[2005 United States Figure Skating Championships|2005 U.S. national]] junior title, and placed sixth at the [[2006 World Junior Figure Skating Championships|2006 World Junior Championships]]. Pratt initially competed with her brother, Robert. She teamed up with [[Todd Gilles]] at the 2002 [[Lake Placid, New York]], dance competition. [[Benjamín Vicuña]] (2015–2021)
[[Mauro Icardi]] (2024-Present) | children = 3 | parents = }} '''María Eugenia Suárez Riveiro''' (born 9 March 1992), better known as '''China Suárez''' or '''La China''', is an Argentine actress, singer, and model. == Early life == María Eugenia Suárez Riveiro was born on March 9, 1992, in [[Buenos Aires, Argentina]]. She is the daughter of Guillermo Suárez and Marcela Riveiro Mitsumori. She has an older brother named Agustín Suárez. Her maternal grandmother, Marta Mitsumori, was born in Argentina, and is of [[Japanese people|Japanese]] descent. During her childhood, Suárez attended the Instituto Corazón de María up to her third year of secondary school and completed her secondary studies at ESBA Barrio Norte. She also attended Divino Corazón de Jesús, located in [[Palermo, Buenos Aires]]. == Career == Suárez made her debut as an actress when she was eleven years old in the television series [[Rincón de Luz|''Rincón de luz'']] (2003), created by [[Cris Morena]], in which she was part of the children's cast. In 2004 she had a small role in the television series ''[[Floricienta]]'' playing the younger sister of Muni Seligmann's character. A year later she appeared in [[Amor mío (Argentine TV series)|''Amor mío'']] (Argentina) and in 2006 in the sitcom ''[[Amo de casa]]''.{{Cite web|url=https://www.diariopopular.com.ar/espectaculos/china-suarez-soy-rebelde-como-mi-personaje-n197228|title=China Suárez: "Soy rebelde como mi personaje"|website=Diario Popular|date=13 July 2014 |language=es-AR|access-date=2020-04-10}} Between 2007 and 2010 Suárez played Jazmín "Jaz" Romero in the television series ''[[Casi Ángeles]]'', also created by [[Cris Morena]], and the theatrical adaptations of the show. From the series arose the musical group [[Teen Angels]], of which Suárez was a member. At the beginning of 2011, Suárez left the band and later received the [[Kids' Choice Awards Argentina 2011|Kids Choice Awards Argentina]] of "favorite actress" for her work in Casi Ángeles.{{Cite web|url=https://exitoina.perfil.com/noticias/destacada/2011-02-02-40146-la-verdad-sobre-la-desvinculacion-de-euge-suarez-de-teen-angels.phtml|title=La verdad sobre la desvinculación de Euge Suárez de Teen Angels|date=2011-02-02|website=Exitoina|language=es|access-date=2020-04-10}}{{Cite web|url=https://exitoina.perfil.com/noticias/de-pasillo/2011-10-12-76250-todos-los-ganadores-de-los-kids-choice-awards.phtml|title=Todos los ganadores de los Kids' Choice Awards|date=2011-10-12|website=Exitoina|language=es|access-date=2020-04-15}} Between 2011 and 2012 Suárez was part of the cast of [[Los únicos|''Los Únicos'']], produced by [[Pol-ka]]. She later starred with [[Nicolás Pauls]] in the miniseries ''[[30 días juntos]],'' aired on [[Cosmopolitan Television|Cosmopolitan TV]] (Latin America).{{Cite web|url=https://www.diariopopular.com.ar/espectaculos/la-china-suarez-dos-amores-su-nueva-ficcion-n130487|title=La China Suárez, entre dos amores en su nueva ficción|website=Diario Popular|date=19 September 2012 |language=es-AR|access-date=2020-04-15}} In 2013 Suárez went back to working with Pol-ka in the comedy ''[[Solamente vos]]'', where she worked with her costar from ''Casi Angeles'', [[Lali Espósito]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/espectaculos/como-fue-el-regreso-de-la-china-suarez-a-solamente-vos-nid1612581|title=Cómo fue el regreso de la China Suárez a Solamente vos|date=2013-08-21|website=lanacion.com.ar|language=es|access-date=2020-04-15}} In 2014 she co-starred in the telenovela ''[[Camino al amor]]'' with [[Mariano Martínez (actor)|Mariano Martínez]], Sebastián Estevanez and [[Carina Zampini]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.infoveloz.com/post/la-china-suarez-y-mariano-martinez-se-casan-y-dejan-camino-al-amor_96801|title=La China Suárez y Mariano Martínez se casan y dejan "Camino al amor"|last=InfoVeloz.com|website=InfoVeloz.com|language=es|access-date=2020-04-15}} Also in 2014, she was invited to star in the second season of ''[[Tu cara me suena (Argentinian TV series)|Tu cara me suena]]'', aired on [[Telefe]], where she imitated [[Nicole Kidman]] from the movie [[Moulin Rouge!]] along with fellow actor [[Fernando Dente]].{{cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/2014/11/09/1607706-la-china-suarez-paso-tu-cara-me-suena-y-cerro-su-actuacion-un-apasionado-beso-fernando-dente/|title=La "China" Suárez pasó por Tu cara me suena y cerró su actuación con un apasionado beso a Fernando Dente|last= |first= |date=9 November 2014|website=Infobae|language=es-ES|access-date=2020-04-15}} Suárez also starred in the music video for ''Hoy'', by [[David Bisbal]].{{cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/2014/06/25/1575794-el-video-que-muestra-juntos-david-bisbal-y-la-china-suarez/|title=El video que muestra juntos a David Bisbal y "la China" Suárez|last= |first= |date=25 June 2014|website=Infobae|language=es-ES|access-date=2020-04-15}} In 2015 Suárez made her first appearance on the big screen with the [[Abzurdah|film adaptation]] of the book [[Abzurdah (book)|''Abzurdah'']].{{Cite web|url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/espectaculos/china-suarez-nunca-tuve-un-amor-enfermizo-nid1798112|title=China Suárez: "Nunca tuve un amor enfermizo "|date=2015-06-04|website=lanacion.com.ar|language=es|access-date=2020-04-15}} She also recorded her own version of the song Trátame suavemente, by [[Soda Stereo]], for the movie.{{Cite web|url=https://www.clarin.com/fama/china_suarez-homenaje-tratame_suavemente-cerati-la-criticaron_0_BkuxbcYwmg.html|title=La China Suárez homenajeó a Cerati y la criticaron sus fans|last=Clarín.com|website=clarin.com|date=6 May 2015 |language=es|access-date=2020-04-15}} For her performance she received the [[Premio Sur]] for as Best New Actress. On July 18, 2015, Suárez served as the ambassador for Argentine cinema at the Premios Platino.{{Cite web|url=https://www.pronto.com.ar/articulo/famosos/china-suarez-elegida-representar-nuestro-pais-europa-enterate-todos-detalles-gran-logro/20150708095049181145.html|title=China Suárez, elegida para representar a nuestro país en Europa: Enterate todos los detalles de su gran logro|last=PRONTO|website=PRONTO|language=es|access-date=2020-04-15|archive-date=11 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150811232948/http://www.pronto.com.ar/articulo/famosos/china-suarez-elegida-representar-nuestro-pais-europa-enterate-todos-detalles-gran-logro/20150708095049181145.html|url-status=dead}} In 2015, she also launched her own clothing line, which includes jackets, blouses, pants, tops, dresses, purses and necklaces.{{Cite web|url=https://www.losandes.com.ar/article/la-china-suarez-lanzo-su-coleccion-de-ropa-imposible-de-comprar|title=La China Suárez lanzó su colección de ropa: imposible de comprar|website=losandes.com.ar|language=es-AR|access-date=2020-04-15}} In 2016 Suárez starred in the romantic comedy ''{{ill|El hilo rojo|es}}'', with costar Benjamín Vicuña and director [[Daniela Goggi]]. She also voice acted the role of Meena in the Argentinian version of the animated film ''[[Sing (2016 American film)|Sing]]''.{{Cite web|url=https://www.fandango.lat/ar/noticias/la-china-suarez-y-leonardo-sbaraglia-pusieron-sus-voces-en-sing-25067|title=La China Suárez y Leonardo Sbaraglia pusieron sus voces en 'Sing' {{!}} Fandango Argentina|website=fandango.lat|language=es-AR|access-date=2020-04-15}} In 2017 Suárez again co-starred with Vicuña in the film ''{{ill|Los padecientes|es|Los padecientes (película de 2017)}}'', directed by Nicolas Tuozzo and based on the novel by {{ill|Gabriel Rolón|es}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/espectaculos/cine/un-thriller-poco-convincente-nid2017831|title=Los padecientes: un thriller que no convence|date=2017-04-27|website=lanacion.com.ar|language=es|access-date=2020-04-15}} In 2019, Suárez returned to the small screen in the historical telenovela: [[Argentina, tierra de amor y venganza|''Argentina, tierra de amor y verganza'']], produced by Pol-ka. There, she played the role of Raquel, a Polish woman that is tricked into traveling to Argentina by the promise of marrying a rich man, when in reality she is brought there for prostitution. Later, Suárez starred in the series ''Tu parte del trato'', where she played a female police officer. == Personal life == In the early 2010s, Suárez was in a relationship with Argentine television and film producer Nacho Viale, the grandson of television host [[Mirtha Legrand]]. The relationship began around 2010 and received significant attention in Argentine entertainment media.{{Cite web |title=La China Suárez reveló un dato inesperado sobre su relación con Nacho Viale |url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/argentina/la-china-suarez-revelo-un-dato-inesperado-sobre-su-relacion-con-nacho-viale-202382103646 |website=El Observador |date=2 August 2023 |language=es |access-date=13 March 2026 }} The couple separated in 2012. From 2012 to 2013, Suárez was in a relationship with Argentine then married actor [[Nicolás Cabré]]{{Cite web |title=La China Suárez y Nicolás Cabré disfrutan en Isla Margarita. |url=https://www.elsol.com.ar/espectaculos/la-china-suarez-y-nicolas-cabre-disfrutan-en-isla-margarita/ |website=El Sol |date=14 November 2012 |language=English |access-date=14 November 2012 }}{{Cite web |title=El Comienzo de la relación entre la China Suárez y Nicolás Cabré. Por Angel de Brito. |url=https://www.infobae.com/teleshow/2026/01/21/el-demoledor-dato-que-dio-angel-de-brito-sobre-la-actitud-de-la-china-suarez-con-eugenial-tobal-antes-de-salir-con-nicolas-cabre// |website=Infobae |date=2012–2026 |language=Spanish |access-date=21 January 2026 }}{{Cite web |title=La dura confesión de Eugenia Tobal sobre la infidelidad de Nicolás Cabré con la China Suárez. |url=https://viapais.com.ar/entretenimiento/la-dura-confesion-de-eugenia-tobal-sobre-la-infidelidad-de-nicolas-cabre-con-la-china-suarez-era-un-cadaver/#google_vignette/ |website=Via Pais |date=6 February 2025 |language=Spanish |access-date=6 February 2025 }} During that period, Cabré was married to actress Eugenia Tobal. The separation between Cabré and Tobal in 2012 occurred amid widespread media speculation regarding the relationship between Cabré and Suárez while the actors were working together on the television series ''Los Únicos''.{{Cite web |title=Salió a la luz el gesto de la China Suárez con Eugenia Tobal a 14 años del escándalo |url=https://tn.com.ar/show/famosos/2026/01/21/salio-a-la-luz-un-llamativo-gesto-de-la-china-suarez-con-eugenia-tobal-que-desato-un-escandalo-en-las-redes/ |website=La Nación |date=25 January 2026 |language=es |access-date=13 March 2026 }} Suárez and Cabré later confirmed their relationship publicly and had one daughter together, born in 2013. The couple subsequently separated. In that period, La China Suárez briefly dated Spanish singer [[David Bisbal]]{{Cite web |title=La actriz argentina "China" Suárez confirma relación con David Bisbal. |url=https://www.diariolasamericas.com/la-actriz-argentina-china-suarez-confirma-relacion-david-bisbal-n2909256/ |website=Diario Las Americas |date=15 June 2014 |language=Spanish |access-date=15 June 2014 }}{{Cite web |title=La historia de amor de David Bisbal y 'La China' Suárez y el motivo de su ruptura |url=https://www.divinity.es/famosos/20240705/historia-amor-david-bisbal-china-suarez-motivo-ruptura-be5m_18_012686761.html/ |website=Divinity España |date=5 July 2014 |language=Spanish |access-date=5 July 2014 }} From 2015 to 2021, Suárez was in a relationship with Chilean actor [[Benjamín Vicuña]], with whom she has two children. The high profile sighting occurred amidst escalating legal friction, directly following news that Icardi was fighting massive alimony and child support demands from Wanda Nara. By openly gathering luxury shopping bags at one of the region's premier high end retailers, the pair fueled intense media backlash, providing opposing legal counsel with highly visible, documented evidence of Icardi's financial solvency and immediate liquidity. In Argentine family courts, such public displays of luxury spending serve as critical circumstantial evidence that can directly undermine a debtor’s claims of financial hardship during ongoing support disputes.{{Cite web|title=La justicia intimó a Mauro Icardi a saldar la deuda de la cuota alimentaria de las hijas que tiene con Wanda Nara|url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/espectaculos/la-justicia-intimo-a-mauro-icardi-a-saldar-la-deuda-de-la-cuota-alimentaria-de-las-hijas-que-tiene-nid27062026/|work=Diario LaNación|language=Spanish |access-date=27 June 2026}} Meanwhile, the legal reality of Mauro Icardi’s free agency combined with China Suárez’s employment fluctuations creates a distinct family law dynamic affecting her previous partner, [[Benjamín Vicuña]]. Vicuña’s primary legal leverage does not stem from Suárez's career status, but from the geographic stability of their shared minors. The official expiration of Mauro Icardi’s multi million euro contract with Galatasaray marked a massive turning point for Vicuña, effectively dismantling Suárez’s legal justification for anchoring the children in Istanbul. Prior to Icardi becoming a free agent, Vicuña faced severe parental friction. Suárez repeatedly subverted their judicially mandated custody schedule arbitrarily extending the children's time in Turkey, missing legal return dates to Argentina, and going as far as to unilaterally enroll the minors in Turkish schools without Vicuña’s required parental consent. The logistical arrangement reached a boiling point when a major media scandal erupted revealing that Suárez had left the children in Turkey solely in the care of hired nannies while she traveled to Europe with Icardi, directly violating her parental duty of care. With Icardi's contract officially over and no legitimate employment binding the family to Turkey, Vicuña successfully halted these cross border violations, legally securing his children's return to their habitual residence and schooling in Argentina. Ironically, [[Mauro Icardi]]'s refusal to sign for his daughter's passports legally established Argentina as the Habitual residence for his biological daughters.{{Cite web|title=Why Mauro Icardi celebrated the Italian ruling regarding his daughters and denied Wanda Nara's version|url=https://derechadiario.com.ar/us/argentina/mauro-icardi-celebrated-italian-failure-daughters-denied-wanda-nara-version/|work=Diario Derecha|language=Spanish |access-date=1 August 2026}} From a sports management and regulatory perspective, Argentina has solidified as the definitive residence for Mauro Icardi and China Suárez following the official closure of the primary international transfer windows. With major global leagues finalizing their rosters and Icardi remaining unsigned, the veteran forward’s status as a free agent effectively grounds his personal and professional logistics within the domestic territory for the upcoming competitive cycle. ==Forced Retirement and commercial boycott== Following the expiration of his contract with Turkey's Galatasaray S.K. on June 30, 2026, the professional career of Mauro Icardi entered a period of profound uncertainty, leaving him formally as a free agent. Despite his goalscoring record, the Argentine forward has experienced severe difficulties signing with a new club due to the heavily negative impact of his off field profile. Various European analysts and specialized media outlets have publicly discouraged his signing; a report published by the sports portal '''Viola Nation''' on August 21, 2026, labeled the player a "one man walking soap opera," strictly advising against his transfer to Italy's Serie A. The article emphasized that constant off pitch distractions, including a complex international legal battle over divorce, child support, and custody of his daughters, travel restrictions, litigation over unpaid rent in Istanbul, and intense media exposure alongside his current partner, actress Eugenia "China" Suárez have buried his professional prospects, turning him into a high risk institutional asset for any top tier club.{{Cite web|url=https://www.violanation.com/serie-a-transfer-news-rumours-calciomercato/22592/4-reasons-to-not-touch-mauro-icardi-with-a-39-and-a-half-foot-pole|title=4 reasons to not touch Mauro Icardi with a 39-and-a-half foot pole|publisher=Viola Nation|date=21 August 2026|access-date=21 August 2026}} Meanwhile, several commercial brands in Argentina have distanced themselves from actress and influencer María Eugenia "China" Suárez. While the situation is often described as an informal "commercial boycott" or the "end of her era as an influencer," the retreat is heavily driven by overwhelming social media backlash and corporate risk management rather than an official, coordinated ban. Following the massive 2021 celebrity scandal involving TV host, actress and singer [[Wanda Nara]] and footballer [[Mauro Icardi]], a few major brands immediately rescinded or chose not to renew their contracts with [[China Suárez]] to avoid public controversy. Suárez subsequently launched legal lawsuits against these companies, claiming that their termination of her contracts caused massive financial and reputational damage.Entertainment journalists on Argentine networks like El Diario de Mariana (DDM) reported that Suárez had virtually lost all of her national brand sponsorships. Marketing and commercial teams reportedly stopped booking her to avoid permanent drama.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mdzol.com/mdz-show/2025/2/8/la-verdad-sobre-las-marcas-que-habrian-bajado-la-china-suarez-de-sus-contratos-por-los-picantes-escandalos-con-wanda-nara-1186749.html|title=La verdad sobre las marcas que habrían bajado a la China Suárez de sus contratos por los picantes escándalos con Wanda Nara|publisher=MDZ|date=8 February 2025|access-date=8 February 2025}} ==Controversy and Road Safety Violation (2026)== In September 2026, Suárez was involved in a highly publicized road safety controversy that resulted in government sanctions. The incident arose after she posted footage on social media from inside [[Mauro Icardi]]'s private gated community, which depicted her unbuckling her seatbelt, climbing onto the car door, and leaning half of her upper body out of the window of a moving vehicle while singing a song by Dua Lipa. The vehicle was being operated by her partner, footballer Mauro Icardi. The video prompted an official intervention by the Ministry of Transportation of the Buenos Aires Province, with the Undersecretariat of Road Policy and Safety publicly condemning the behavior as reckless and negligent. '''Shiloh Fernandez''' (born February 26, 1985<ref name="dob"/>) is an American actor. He is known for his roles in the television series ''[[Jericho (2006 TV series)|Jericho]]'' and ''[[United States of Tara]]'', and the films ''[[Deadgirl (2008 film)|Deadgirl]]'' and ''[[Red Riding Hood (2011 film)|Red Riding Hood]]'', as well as for playing David Allen in the 2013 film ''[[Evil Dead (2013 film)|Evil Dead]]'' and the 2022 video game ''[[Evil Dead: The Game]]''.

==Early life==
Fernandez was born in [[Ukiah, California]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Bay City News Service|title=Up-And-Coming Ukiah-Born Actor Shiloh Fernandez Talks About His Role In A Steamy Remake Of A ‘Lost’ Thriller|date=May 13, 2022|website=San Fransicco Gate|url=https://www.sfgate.com/news/bayarea/article/Up-And-Coming-Ukiah-Born-Actor-Shiloh-Fernandez-17170061.php|accessdate=February 12, 2025|archive-date=June 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220616034420/https://www.sfgate.com/news/bayarea/article/Up-And-Coming-Ukiah-Born-Actor-Shiloh-Fernandez-17170061.php|url-status=live}}</ref> Fernandez's father is of half [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] and half [[History of the Jews in Russia|Russian Jewish]] descent, whereas his mother has [[Britons|British]] ancestry.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.latina.com/entertainment/buzz/15-more-stars-you-thought-were-latino-arent?slide=9|title=15 MORE Stars You Thought Were Latino—But Aren't!|date=October 6, 2011|work=[[Latina (magazine)|Latina]]|accessdate=10 November 2012|archive-date=11 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200711092512/http://www.latina.com/entertainment/buzz/15-more-stars-you-thought-were-latino-arent?slide=9|url-status=live}}</ref> He has a younger sister and a brother.<ref name="da man"/> His [[stepfather]] is a [[General contractor|contractor]].<ref name="next"/> Before becoming an actor, Fernandez began working as a [[dishwashing|dishwasher]], and an [[American Apparel]] catalog [[model (person)|model]] hand-picked by the company's CEO, [[Dov Charney]], for his then-fledgling company. Later arriving in [[Los Angeles]], he asked Charney for a job and was hired as a stock boy.<ref name="Interview"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://magnificentobsession.typepad.com/blog/2011/02/printed-matter-shiloh-fernandez-in-nylon-guys.html|title=Printed Matter: Shiloh Fernandez in Nylon Guys|publisher=Magnificent Obsession|accessdate=11 April 2011|archive-date=20 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110820114242/http://magnificentobsession.typepad.com/blog/2011/02/printed-matter-shiloh-fernandez-in-nylon-guys.html|url-status=live}}</ref> His first acting gig was a commercial for First 5 California that was directed by [[Vadim Perelman]].<ref name="next"/>

==Career==
===2006–10: early work===
After completing a short film, Fernandez made his debut television appearance in a 2006 episode of ''[[Cold Case]]'', followed by minor roles in ''[[Drake & Josh]]'' and ''[[Lincoln Heights (TV series)|Lincoln Heights]]''.<ref name="next"/><ref name="female">{{cite web|url=http://www.femalefirst.co.uk/movies/Introducing+Shiloh+Fernandez-10043.html|title=Introducing Shiloh Fernandez|first=Helen|last=Earnshaw|date=12 April 2011|publisher=Female First|accessdate=3 May 2011|archive-date=14 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110414123245/http://www.femalefirst.co.uk/movies/Introducing+Shiloh+Fernandez-10043.html|url-status=live}}</ref> His screen debut came two years later, in 2007, when he landed the role of Edgar in ''Interstate'' before returning to TV. He landed his first recurring role in ''[[Jericho (2006 TV series)|Jericho]]'' as Sean Henthorn between 2006 and 2007. The series was cancelled after just one season before a campaign by fans saw it return for a second before being cancelled once again.<ref name="female"/>

In 2008, Fernandez became one of the front-runners to play [[Edward Cullen]] after he auditioned for [[Catherine Hardwicke]] in her [[Venice, Los Angeles|Venice Beach]] garage, during the casting of ''[[Twilight (2008 film)|Twilight]]''.<ref name="sf"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ok.co.uk/celebnews/view/13285/Ben-Jackson-Shiloh-all-auditioned-for-R-Pattz-s-Edward-Cullen-role-/|title=Ben, Jackson & Shiloh all auditioned for Robert Pattinson's Edward Cullen role|date=20 August 2009|work=[[OK!]]|accessdate=6 April 2011|archive-date=23 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110623152408/http://www.ok.co.uk/celebnews/view/13285/Ben-Jackson-Shiloh-all-auditioned-for-R-Pattz-s-Edward-Cullen-role-/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Fernandez was allegedly Hardwicke's first choice, but it was up to [[Kristen Stewart]] who had the last say. Shiloh later recalled on his narrowly missed opportunity, "At the time, it was just another audition. I didn't realize I was missing out on stardom and giant paychecks. Now, looking back on it, I certainly wouldn't have been mentally stable enough to deal with all that. Lucky for me, not getting that part led to other work that was a much better fit for me."<ref name="VMan">{{cite web|url=http://www.vman.com/articles/shiloh-fernandez-new-teen-idol/|title=Shiloh Fernandez: New Teen Idol|last=Cole|first=Rachel T.|date=27 January 2011|work=[[VMAN]]|accessdate=8 April 2011|archive-date=9 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120909054242/http://www.vman.com/articles/shiloh-fernandez-new-teen-idol/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Fernandez, who had no formal training, admitted being bashful around other actors during rehearsals.<ref name="sf"/>  He did an array of television shows (''[[CSI: NY]]'', ''[[The United States of Tara]]'') including starring in the ''[[Gossip Girl]]'' episode "[[Valley Girls]]" as Owen Campos, alongside [[Brittany Snow]] and [[Krysten Ritter]]. He eventually landed his first big break playing a troubled small-town Texas rink manager in the 2010 [[Sundance Film Festival|Sundance]] hit ''[[Skateland]]'' with ''Twilight'' alum [[Ashley Greene]].<ref name="sf">{{cite web|url=http://www.sfexaminer.com/entertainment/movies/2011/03/shiloh-fernandez-lookin-good|title=Shiloh Fernandez is lookin' good|last=Drake|first=Rossiter|date=6 March 2011|work=[[The San Francisco Examiner]]|accessdate=7 March 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716052913/http://www.sfexaminer.com/entertainment/movies/2011/03/shiloh-fernandez-lookin-good|archivedate=16 July 2011}}</ref><ref name="VMan"/>

In 2013, Fernandez starred in the remake of ''[[Evil Dead (2013 film)|Evil Dead]]'' and in the independent film ''[[Syrup (film)|Syrup]]'', based on the [[Syrup (novel)|novel of the same name]] by [[Max Barry]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.variety.com/article/VR1118036658?refCatId=13|title=Shiloh Fernandez, Amber Heard pour 'Syrup'|last=Kroll|first=Justin|date=9 May 2011|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|accessdate=14 May 2011|archive-date=13 May 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110513102411/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1118036658?refCatId=13|url-status=live}}</ref> In March 2015, Fernandez landed a role in the Canadian thriller film ''[[Edge of Winter (film)|Edge of Winter]]'', starring [[Rossif Sutherland]], [[Joel Kinnaman]], [[Tom Holland (actor)|Tom Holland]], Percy Hynes-White and [[Rachelle Lefevre]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/93765/evil-deads-shiloh-fernandez-and-more-head-to-backcountry/|title=Evil Dead's Shiloh Fernandez and More Head to Backcountry|first=Steve|last=Barton|date=March 18, 2015|website=Dread Central|access-date=April 21, 2020|archive-date=August 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822210915/http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/93765/evil-deads-shiloh-fernandez-and-more-head-to-backcountry/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His favorite movie of all time is ''[[The Thing Called Love]]'' and [[River Phoenix]] is his idol.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nextmovie.com/blog/shiloh-fernandez-favorite-movie/|title=My Favorite Movie: Shiloh Fernandez|last=DeSalvo|first=Robert|date=12 March 2011|publisher=Next Movie|accessdate=10 April 2011|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304053908/http://www.nextmovie.com/blog/shiloh-fernandez-favorite-movie/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Fernandez has stated that if he were not acting, he would have [[Academic major|majored]] in [[Spanish language|Spanish]], moved to [[South America]], and run a banana farm or worked in [[construction]], because he is good with his hands; or, if he was better at it, a [[Writing|writer]]. Fernandez has an affinity for [[country music]], and his dream role is to play a country music star.<ref name="next">{{cite web|url=http://www.nextmovie.com/blog/next-factor-shiloh-fernandez/|title=Next Factor: Shiloh Fernandez|last=DeSalvo|first=Robert|date=9 March 2011|publisher=Next Movie|accessdate=10 April 2011|archive-date=3 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303230716/http://www.nextmovie.com/blog/next-factor-shiloh-fernandez/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a friend of actor [[Thomas Dekker (actor)|Thomas Dekker]].<ref name="movieline"/> He married his longtime girlfriend Emily Tremaine during a ceremony on October 8, 2022 at the Cavalli Estate in San Luis Obispo, California.

{{Short description|American football coach (born 1986)}} {{For|the Irish sportsman|Seán McVeigh}} {{Use American English|date=September 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2025}} {{Infobox gridiron football biography | name = Sean McVay | image = Sean McVay 2019 (cropped2).jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = McVay with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in 2019 | current_team = Los Angeles Rams | position = [[Head coach]] | career_position =wr | career_number = | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1986|1|24|mf=y}} | birth_place = [[Dayton, Ohio]], U.S. | high_school = [[Marist School (Georgia)|Marist]] ([[Brookhaven, Georgia]]) | college = [[Miami RedHawks football|Miami (OH)]] (2004–2008) | pastcoaching = * [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] ({{nfly|2008}})
Offensive assistant * [[Florida Tuskers]] (2009)
Wide receivers coach * {{ubl|[[Washington Redskins]] ({{nfly|2010|2016}})}} ** {{ubl|Offensive assistant ({{nfly|2010}})}} ** {{ubl|Tight ends coach ({{nfly|2011|2013}})}} ** {{ubl|Offensive coordinator ({{nfly|2014|2016}})}} * [[Los Angeles Rams]] ({{nfly|2017}}–present)
Head coach | highlights = * [[List of Super Bowl champions|Super Bowl champion]] ([[Super Bowl LVI|LVI]]) * [[AP NFL Coach of the Year]] ({{NFL Year|2017}}) ;NFL records * Youngest head coach hired in NFL history: 30 * Youngest head coach to reach the Super Bowl: 33 * Youngest head coach to win the Super Bowl: 36 | regular_record = {{Winning percentage|94|59|record=y}} | playoff_record = {{Winning percentage|10|6|record=y}} | overall_record = {{Winning percentage|104|65|record=y}} | pfrcoach = McVaSe0 }} '''Sean Patrick McVay'''{{Cite web |title=Sean McVay Record, Statistics, and Category Ranks |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/coaches/McVaSe0.htm |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} (born January 24, 1986) is an American professional [[American football|football]] coach who is the [[head coach]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He became the youngest NFL head coach in the modern era when he was hired by the Rams in 2017 at the age of 30 years and 353 days. McVay is also the youngest head coach to reach and win a [[Super Bowl]] as well as be named [[AP NFL Coach of the Year Award|NFL Coach of the Year]]. Prior to his tenure in Los Angeles, McVay worked with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as an offensive assistant, the [[Florida Tuskers]] as the wide receivers coach, and the [[Washington Redskins]] as an offensive assistant, the tight ends coach, and the offensive coordinator. Within his first year, McVay turned a Rams team that had the league's lowest scoring offense the previous year into the top-scoring team of 2017. The season also marked the Rams' first winning record and division title since 2003 and first playoff appearance since 2004. Over the following seasons, McVay led the Rams to an appearance in [[Super Bowl LIII]] in 2019, a victory in [[Super Bowl LVI]] in 2022, the franchise's first championship since 1999, and became the winningest head coach in Rams' history in 2024. His success in Los Angeles is credited with spawning the "[[Sean McVay effect]]", in which NFL teams were more inclined to hire younger, offensive-minded head coaches. ==Early life and family== Sean Patrick McVay was born on January 24, 1986, in [[Dayton, Ohio]], the son of Tim and Cindy McVay.{{Cite web |last=Bovenzi |first=Tino |date=February 10, 2022 |title='Proud of my roots': Rams coach Sean McVay's deep ties to Ohio |url=https://spectrumnews1.com/oh/columbus/sports/2022/02/10/rams-mcvay-has-deep-ties-to-ohio |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220215230210/https://spectrumnews1.com/oh/columbus/sports/2022/02/10/rams-mcvay-has-deep-ties-to-ohio |archive-date=February 15, 2022 |access-date=February 15, 2022 |website=[[Spectrum News 1]]}}{{Cite web |date=January 12, 2017 |title=Miami grad, Dayton native Sean McVay becomes youngest coach in NFL history |url=https://www.journal-news.com/sports/cradle-coaches-produces-another-one-sean-mcvay/WH0v8qzyGmTpgLn56ofMaO/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220215232237/https://www.journal-news.com/sports/cradle-coaches-produces-another-one-sean-mcvay/WH0v8qzyGmTpgLn56ofMaO/ |archive-date=February 15, 2022 |access-date=February 15, 2022 |website=The Journal-News}} Tim played football as a defensive back at [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana University]], where he was a two-time team captain. Tim and Cindy met when they were both students at Indiana, and they got married in 1981. Tim embarked on a successful career spanning four decades as a television executive for [[Cox Communications]], and Cindy became an interior designer. The McVay family lived in Dayton until Sean was six years old, and they eventually settled in the [[Atlanta, Georgia]], area.{{Cite web |last1=Thiry |first1=Lindsey |last2=Schlabach |first2=Mark |author-link2=Mark Schlabach |date=January 31, 2019 |title=An inside look at Rams coach Sean McVay's Super Bowl homecoming |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles-rams/post/_/id/39893/sean-mcvays-super-bowl-homecoming-broken-noses-and-a-beat-up-lexus |access-date=November 14, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Tim McVay College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/tim-mcvay-1.html |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}{{cite web | title=2018 GAB Hall of Fame Inductee Tim McVay | website=Georgia Association of Broadcasters | date=2018-01-20 | url=https://www.gab.org/2018-gab-hall-of-fame-inductee-tim-mcvay/ | access-date=2026-02-22}}{{cite web | last=Engelhardt | first=Gordon | title=Super Bowl 56: Mom of Rams coach, referee have ties to Evansville | website=Courier & Press | date=2022-02-10 | url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/2022/02/10/super-bowl-56-mom-rams-coach-referee-have-ties-evansville/9285132002/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-epti=z113925d00----v113925d--39--b--39--&gca-ft=152&gca-ds=sophi&gnt-djm=1 | access-date=2026-02-20}} Sean's paternal grandfather, [[John McVay|John]], was a longtime football coach at the high school, college, and professional levels. Most notably, he was the head coach for the [[Dayton Flyers football|University of Dayton]], the [[Memphis Southmen]] of the [[World Football League]], and the NFL's [[New York Giants]], before transitioning into front office roles. John served as an executive for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] between 1980 and 1999, winning the NFL's Executive of the Year award for the team's successful [[1989 San Francisco 49ers|1989 season]].{{Cite web |title=John McVay Record, Statistics, and Category Ranks |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/coaches/McVaJo0.htm |access-date=November 14, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Manzano |first=Gilbert |date=November 2, 2022 |title=Rams coach Sean McVay remembers his grandfather, former 49ers GM John McVay |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/11/02/rams-coach-sean-mcvay-remembers-his-grandfather-former-49ers-gm-john-mcvay |access-date=November 14, 2022 |website=Orange County Register |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=January 12, 2017 |title=Three Things to Know about Rams HC Sean McVay |url=https://www.therams.com/news/three-things-to-know-about-rams-hc-sean-mcvay-18434764 |access-date=January 12, 2017 |website=therams.com}} ===High school football=== McVay attended and graduated from [[Marist High School (Georgia)|Marist School]] in [[Brookhaven, Georgia]] in 2004. He was a four-year starter at Marist as a [[quarterback]] and safety for the War Eagles [[high school football]] team and the first player in school history to amass 1,000 yards rushing and passing in consecutive seasons. McVay totaled 2,600 yards rushing and 40 rushing [[touchdown]]s during his career and also passed for 2,500 yards and 18 touchdowns, leading the War Eagles to a 26–3 record, including a 14–1 record and state championship his senior year, when McVay was also named the Georgia 4A Offensive Player of the Year over future NFL Hall of Fame wide receiver [[Calvin Johnson]].{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=January 6, 2018 |title=Sean McVay once beat out Calvin Johnson for Player of the Year in high school |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2018/01/06/nfl-los-angeles-rams-sean-mcvay-calvin-johnson-player-of-the-year-high-school/ |access-date=November 13, 2022 |website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today}} ==College career== McVay attended [[Miami University]] in [[Oxford, Ohio]], where he played [[college football]] as a [[wide receiver]] from 2005 to 2007, earning Miami's Scholar-Athlete Award in 2007. Playing in 26 games over three seasons, McVay recorded 39 receptions for 312 yards for the RedHawks in his college career.{{Cite web |title=Sean McVay College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/sean-mcvay-1.html |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}} He graduated from Miami in 2008 with a B.S. in Health and Sports Studies. ===College statistics=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" |- ! rowspan="2"| Year ! rowspan="2"| Team ! colspan="4"| Receiving ! colspan="4"| Rushing |- ! }} ===Washington Redskins (2010–2016)=== [[File: Sean McVay 2014 (cropped).jpg |thumb|McVay in 2014|308x308px]] In 2010, McVay was hired as the assistant tight ends coach for the [[Washington Redskins]] under head coach [[Mike Shanahan]]. The following season, McVay was promoted to tight ends coach, a position he held through the [[2013 Washington Redskins season|2013 season]].{{Cite news |last=Allen |first=Scott |date=January 8, 2019 |title=Mike Shanahan's 2013 Redskins staff has produced as many NFL head coaches as wins |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/01/08/mike-shanahans-redskins-staff-has-produced-many-nfl-head-coaches-wins/ |access-date=February 8, 2019 |newspaper=Washington Post |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Gonzalez |first=Alden |date=September 20, 2017 |title=49ers' Kyle Shanahan, Rams' Sean McVay are forever linked |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles-rams/post/_/id/35429 |access-date=February 8, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} During these years, McVay coached multiple tights ends such as [[Chris Cooley]], [[Fred Davis (tight end)|Fred Davis]], [[Logan Paulsen]], and [[Jordan Reed]]. On January 14, 2014, McVay was promoted to offensive coordinator by new head coach Jay Gruden. He would succeed his future NFC West coaching rival [[Kyle Shanahan]] in that role.{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=January 14, 2014 |title=Sean McVay becomes offensive coordinator in Washington |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/sean-mcvay-becomes-offensive-coordinator-in-washington |access-date=February 22, 2026 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}} Over the next three seasons, McVay had a direct impact in developing [[Kirk Cousins]] into a franchise quarterback. Becoming the full-time starter in [[2015 Washington Redskins season|2015]], Cousins led the Redskins to back-to-back winning seasons, throwing for over 9,000 yards and more than 50 touchdowns under McVay's direction. In [[2016 Washington Redskins season|2016]], Cousins was named to the [[Pro Bowl]] for the first time. McVay's success with Cousins made him an attractive head coaching candidate and following the season, McVay was interviewed by both the [[Los Angeles Rams]] and the [[San Francisco 49ers]].{{cite web | title=49ers Interview Sean McVay for Head Coach | website=49ers.com| date=2017-01-09 | url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-interview-sean-mcvay-for-head-coach-18418596 | access-date=2026-02-22}} ===Los Angeles Rams (2017–present)=== ====2017 season: NFL Coach of the Year==== {{See also|2017 Los Angeles Rams season}} On January 12, 2017, McVay was hired by owner [[Stan Kroenke]] to become the 28th head coach of the [[Los Angeles Rams]] at the age of {{age in years and days|1986|1|24|2017|1|12}}. The hiring made McVay the youngest head coach in the NFL's modern era, surpassing [[Lane Kiffin]], who was {{age in years and days|1975|5|9|2007|1|23}} old when hired by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in 2007,{{Cite web |last=Klein |first=Gary |date=January 12, 2017 |title=Rams have a new leading man in Coach Sean McVay |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/la-sp-rams-sean-mcvay-20170112-story.html |access-date=January 12, 2017 |website=Los Angeles Times}} and the youngest since 27-year-old [[Art Lewis]] became interim head coach of the then-Cleveland Rams in 1938.{{Cite web |last=Connley |first=Courtney |date=January 18, 2019 |title=Los Angeles Rams' Sean McVay is the youngest NFL head coach to lead a team to the Super Bowl |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/01/18/how-la-rams-sean-mcvay-became-the-youngest-head-coach-in-the-nfl.html |access-date=February 4, 2019 |publisher=[[CNBC]]}} McVay would remain the youngest head coach in the NFL until the [[New England Patriots]] hired [[Jerod Mayo]] on January 12, 2024, exactly seven years to the day after McVay was hired by the Rams.{{Cite web |last=Dubin |first=Jared |date=January 12, 2024 |title=Patriots' Jerod Mayo becomes new youngest coach in NFL, ending Sean McVay's seven-year run |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/patriots-jerod-mayo-becomes-new-youngest-coach-in-nfl-ending-sean-mcvays-seven-year-run/ |access-date=January 27, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en-US}} McVay inherited a Rams team that finished [[2016 NFL season|2016]] in last place in points, total yards, touchdown passes and first downs, a team later ranked as having the second-worst offense of the decade based on [[Football Outsiders]]' DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average) statistic.{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=June 17, 2020 |title=2016 Rams ranked as one of the worst offenses of the decade |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2020/06/17/nfl-rams-worst-offense-decade-espn/ |access-date=October 25, 2022 |website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}} On January 19, 2017, veteran coach [[Wade Phillips]] was hired by McVay as defensive coordinator.{{Cite web |last=Beacham |first=Greg |date=January 19, 2017 |title=LA Rams confirm Wade Phillips hired as defensive coordinator |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2017/01/19/la-rams-confirm-wade-phillips-hired-as-defensive-coordinator/ |access-date=January 27, 2024 |website=DenverPost.com |language=en-US}} On February 8, McVay hired [[Matt LaFleur]] as his [[offensive coordinator]]. LaFleur had previously worked with McVay in Washington when McVay was tight ends coach and LaFleur was quarterbacks coach.{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 8, 2017 |title=Rams name Matt LaFleur offensive coordinator |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-name-matt-lafleur-offensive-coordinator-0ap3000000784668 |access-date=February 10, 2017 |website=NFL.com}} Following a 2–2 preseason, on September 10, 2017, McVay made his regular-season head coaching debut against the [[2017 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] and led the Rams to a 46–9 victory in a home game at the [[Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum]].{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Los Angeles Rams – September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100ram.htm |access-date=October 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}} After a 27–20 loss in Week 2 to McVay's former team, the [[2017 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]], the Rams pulled off a narrow 41–39 road victory over the [[2017 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]] on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]''.{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at San Francisco 49ers – September 21st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709210sfo.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} During Week 4, the Rams turned a 16–24 deficit into a 35–30 upset road victory over the [[2017 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]], but they lost their next game to their [[NFC West]] division rival [[2017 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] at home by a score of 16–10. Regardless, in just five games, the Rams scored a total of 152 points, a dramatic and immediate improvement (Los Angeles had only scored 82 total points through its first five games in [[2016 Los Angeles Rams season|2016]]). They went on to beat the [[2017 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] on the road by a score of 27–17 in Week 6 and the [[2017 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]] by a score of 33–0 in an [[NFL International Series]] game at [[London]]'s [[Twickenham Stadium]] for the team's first shutout win since [[2014 St. Louis Rams season|2014]], as well as raising their record to 5–2 for the first time since [[2004 St. Louis Rams season|2004]] (the last time the team made the playoffs){{Cite web |title=Cleveland/St. Louis/LA Rams Team Encyclopedia |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/ram/index.htm |access-date=February 8, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} and a first-place lead in the [[NFC West]]. McVay coached the Rams to a blowout victory against the [[2017 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] in their highest-scoring game, a 51–17 road rout that raised the Rams' record to 6–2. The Rams would win another home game against the [[2017 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]] by a score of 33–7 to raise their record to 7–2, the team's best start since [[2001 St. Louis Rams season|2001]].{{cite web | title=Jared Goff leads Rams to 4th straight win, 33-7 over Texans | website=ESPN | date=November 12, 2017|agency=Associated Press| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/400951663 | access-date=2026-02-22}} In Weeks 11 and 12, the Rams lost to the [[2017 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] on the road by a score of 24–7 but won at home against the [[2017 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]] 26–20 to raise their record to 8–3. With a 32–16 road victory over the Cardinals in Week 13, the Rams achieved their first winning season since [[2003 St. Louis Rams season|2003]].{{Cite web |date=December 3, 2017 |title=Rams special teams shine in win over Cardinals |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2017/12/03/rams-special-teams-shine-in-win-over-cardinals/108294992/ |access-date=February 8, 2019 |website=USAToday.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}} Although they lost to the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] 43–35 at home in Week 14, the Rams had two victories in Week 15 and Week 16. Running back [[Todd Gurley]] had 456 yards in total offense with six touchdowns to lead Los Angeles in back-to-back wins on the road over the [[2017 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] 42–7 and then the [[2017 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] 27–23 road victory, the latter of which secured for the Rams the [[NFC West]] title. McVay's first season with the Rams saw them dramatically improve their record from the 2016 season, finishing with the team's first winning season and division title since [[2003 St. Louis Rams season|2003]] and its first playoff berth since [[2004 St. Louis Rams season|2004]]. In the process, Los Angeles became the first team to have the top scoring offense in the league a year after finishing with the lowest scoring offense.{{Cite web |last=Parzych |first=Dan |date=January 2, 2018 |title=Rams making history by going from worst to first in scoring is truly amazing |url=https://ramblinfan.com/2018/01/02/rams-making-history-going-worst-first-scoring-truly-amazing/ |access-date=February 8, 2019 |website=Ramblin' Fan|publisher=FanSided |language=en-US}} McVay made his playoff head coaching debut against the [[2017 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]], but the Rams lost at home in the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#NFC: Atlanta Falcons 26, Los Angeles Rams 13|Wild Card Round]] by a score of 26–13.{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Atlanta Falcons at Los Angeles Rams – January 6th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801060ram.htm |access-date=February 8, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} On January 19, 2018, at the The Rams started the season 3–0, winning against the [[2019 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]], [[2019 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]], and [[2019 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]]. However, they then lost three straight to the [[2019 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[2019 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], and [[2019 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]]. Before a Week 9 bye, they won two games against the [[2019 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] and [[2019 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]]. The Rams then won four and lost four. The team faced problems during the season due to a combination of factors and lost in heartbreaking fashion on the road by a score of 34–31 against the 49ers, which eliminated the Rams from the playoffs.{{cite web | last=DaSilva | first=Cameron | title=Rams eliminated from playoff contention after 34-31 loss to 49ers | website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today| date=2019-12-22 | url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/rams/2019/12/21/nfl-rams-playoffs-week-16-eliminated-49ers/80809192007/ | access-date=2026-02-22}}{{Cite web |title=2019 Los Angeles Rams Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/ram/2019.htm |access-date=November 14, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Los Angeles finished the season at 9–7 with a season-ending 31–24 victory over the [[2019 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]] in the team's final game at the [[Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum]].{{cite web | last=Jackson | first=Stu | title=Game Recap: Rams send off Coliseum, season with 31-24 win over Cardinals | website=therams.com | date=2019-12-30 | url=https://www.therams.com/news/game-recap-rams-cardinals-week-17 | access-date=2026-02-22}} ====2020 season==== {{See also|2020 Los Angeles Rams season}} After a victory over the [[2020 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] in the season opener, the Rams started off the first half of the 2020 season going 5–3, with wins over the [[2020 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], [[2020 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], [[2020 Washington Football Team season|Washington Football Team]], and [[2020 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]]. However, they lost to the [[2020 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]], [[2020 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]], and [[2020 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. The Rams finished the season with a 10–6 record with wins over the [[2020 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], [[2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[2020 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], and [[2020 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]]. [[Les Snead]] had signed extensions with the team, keeping them with the franchise through the 2026 season.{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=September 8, 2022 |title=Rams coach Sean McVay, GM Les Snead sign contract extensions through 2026 season |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-coach-sean-mcvay-gm-les-snead-sign-contract-extensions-through-2026-season |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=NFL.com}} McVay and the Rams would host the [[Buffalo Bills]] in their first game for the 2022 season, where they unveiled their Super Bowl championship banner at [[SoFi Stadium]].{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=September 8, 2022 |title=Rams unveil Super Bowl LVI banner at SoFi Stadium |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2022/09/08/rams-super-bowl-banner-sofi-stadium-bills/ |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=Rams Wire}} The Rams would lose 31–10, in what would be the first time McVay would lose a season opener, and the first time he would have an active season record under .500.{{Cite web |last=Kerr |first=Jeff |date=September 8, 2022 |title=Sean McVay falls below .500 in regular season for first time in career after Rams season-opening loss to Bills |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/sean-mcvay-falls-below-500-in-regular-season-for-first-time-in-career-after-rams-season-opening-loss-to-bills/ |access-date=January 10, 2023 |publisher=[[CBSSports.com]]}} McVay and the Rams struggled to defend their title throughout the season, as the team lost key members [[Matthew Stafford]], [[Cooper Kupp]], and [[Aaron Donald]] to injury for significant portions of the year. Injuries led to the team turning to former #1 overall pick [[Baker Mayfield]] to start at quarterback for the rest of the season.{{Cite web |date=December 6, 2022 |title=Rams get Baker Mayfield on waivers |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/rams-get-baker-mayfield-on-waivers |access-date=May 29, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}} Mayfield finished the year with a 2–3 record with wins coming against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] on [[Thursday Night Football]] and the [[Denver Broncos]] on [[NFL on Christmas Day|Christmas]].{{Cite web |last=Sutelan |first=Edward |date=December 23, 2022 |title=Where is Aaron Donald? When Rams star is expected to return after injury |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/rams-aaron-donald-star-return-injury/u1lrxzyjl5ef5otkbqyafsy0 |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=[[Sporting News]] |language=en}} However, with consecutive road losses to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] and [[Seattle Seahawks]], the Rams finished 5–12 and missed the playoffs in McVay's first losing season as a head coach.{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=January 9, 2023 |title=Sean McVay mulls immediate future with Rams but 'not done coaching' |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35414228/sean-mcvay-mulls-immediate-future-rams-not-done-coaching |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ====2023 season==== {{See also|2023 Los Angeles Rams season}} With the Rams having traded significant draft capital and given notably high contracts to pursue their Super Bowl championship, many predicted that a team rebuild loomed during the offseason. Despite McVay having signed an extension prior to the previous season, speculation arose that McVay would not want to take part in a rebuild and would instead step away from the team before the next season began.{{Cite web |last=Paris |first=Jay |date=January 9, 2023 |title=Sean McVay's Way Could Be The Highway As The Los Angeles Rams Coach Considers Stepping Away |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jayparis/2023/01/09/sean-mcvays-way-could-be-the-highway-as-the-los-angeles-rams-coach-considers-stepping-away/?sh=63c19d98343b |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=[[Forbes]]}}{{Cite web |last=DelVecchio |first=Steve |date=January 10, 2023 |title=Reason Sean McVay wants to leave Rams revealed? |url=https://larrybrownsports.com/football/reason-sean-mcvay-wants-to-leave-rams/609949 |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=Larry Brown Sports}}{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Sanjesh |date=January 7, 2023 |title=Sean McVay considering stepping away from Rams |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/report-sean-mcvay-considering-stepping-away-rams |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=[[NBC Sports]]}} McVay would later reveal that he had considered stepping away from coaching, as the constant losing during the previous season had taken its toll, but his wife convinced him to stay.{{Cite web |last=Schwab |first=Frank |title=Rams’ Sean McVay on nearly stepping away after 2022 season: ‘I was quitting because I couldn’t handle the losing’ |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/article/rams-sean-mcvay-on-nearly-stepping-away-after-2022-season-i-was-quitting-because-i-couldnt-handle-the-losing-154356272.html |website=Yahoo Sports |date=May 19, 2026 |access-date=May 19, 2026}} Shortly after the regular season finished, sources stated that McVay would return as head coach for the next season.{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=January 13, 2023 |title=Sean McVay tells Rams he's staying as coach |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35440229/sean-mcvay-tells-rams-staying-coach-sources-say |access-date=January 13, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Throughout the offseason, media outlets ruminated over the Rams' dismal 2022 season, and with the team handling $75 million in dead cap money along with a roster filled with first- and second-year players, few outside the franchise organization expected the team to compete for the playoffs.{{Cite web |last=Schwab |first=Frank |date=September 7, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Rams 2023 NFL Preview: 'Boring' Rams take foot off the gas after awful Super Bowl defense |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/los-angeles-rams-2023-nfl-preview-boring-rams-take-foot-off-the-gas-after-awful-super-bowl-defense-175726859.html |access-date=January 27, 2024 |website=sports.yahoo.com |language=en}} A winless (0–3) preseason in which the Rams were outscored 109–34 did little to dispel the pundits' pessimism. The Rams opened the season with a surprisingly strong 30–13 rout of host [[Seattle Seahawks|Seattle]].{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=September 10, 2023 |title=Matthew Stafford throws for 334 yards, Rams dominate Seahawks 30–13 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/matthew-stafford-throws-for-334-yards-rams-dominate-seahawks-30-13 |access-date=May 29, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}} Although Los Angeles dropped three of its next four games against [[San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco]] (30–23), [[Cincinnati Bengals|Cincinnati]] (19–16), and [[Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia]] (23–14), the Rams displayed unexpected resilience against a trio of teams widely expected to contend for the [[Super Bowl]]. The emergence of rookie wide receiver [[Puka Nacua]] and second-year running back [[Kyren Williams]] propelled Los Angeles to a 29–23 overtime victory at [[Indianapolis Colts|Indianapolis]] in Week 4 and a 26–9 rout of [[Arizona Cardinals|Arizona]] at home in Week 6 to even the Rams' record at 3–3. But Williams suffered a severe ankle sprain that sidelined him on injured reserve for a month, and that, combined with injuries to quarterback [[Matthew Stafford]] and wide receiver [[Cooper Kupp]], hampered the Rams who dropped three straight games going into the bye week. Los Angeles returned from the break and gutted out a 17–16 victory over Seattle, then crushed Arizona (37–14) and Cleveland (36–19) before falling 37–31 to the AFC-leading [[Baltimore Ravens]] on the road. With Williams surpassing 1,000 yards rushing, Nacua setting numerous NFL rookie receiving records and the impressive play of rookie defensive stars [[Kobie Turner]] at nose tackle and [[Byron Young (linebacker)|Byron Young]] at linebacker, the Rams rolled to four straight victories to end the season. Back-to-back home victories against [[Washington Commanders|Washington]] (28–20) and [[New Orleans Saints|New Orleans]] (30–22) were followed by a narrow 26–25 victory over the [[New York Giants]] that clinched a playoff berth (McVay's fifth in seven seasons), and a 21–20 win in Week 18 at [[San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco]] that ended a nine-game regular season losing streak to L.A.'s northern California nemesis. The Rams' 10–7 record improved McVay's regular season win total to 70 and overall win total (including playoffs) to 77, both second-most in franchise history behind [[John Robinson (American football coach)|John Robinson]]. Shortly after Los Angeles had clinched a playoff berth, McVay publicly declared that he intended to return as the team's head coach for the [[2024 Los Angeles Rams season|2024 season]].{{Cite web |last=Schwab |first=Frank |date=January 2, 2024 |title=Sean McVay 'promises' return to Rams in 2024 |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/sean-mcvay-promises-return-rams-2024-2024-01-02/ |access-date=January 27, 2024 |website=reuters.com |language=en}} During the Wild Card Round at [[Ford Field]], the Rams narrowly lost 24–23 to the host [[Detroit Lions]], in what marked in Detroit's first playoff win [[1991 Detroit Lions season|in 32 seasons]].{{Cite web |date=January 15, 2024 |title=Jared Goff leads Lions to first playoff win in 32 years, 24–23 over Matthew Stafford and the Rams |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/401547753 |access-date=January 19, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} Following the game, McVay gave much praise to his team, which defied most expectations in reaching the playoffs in what many considered to be a rebuilding year. Following the end of the season, McVay stated: "Man, did I learn a lot and really appreciate this group. They helped me find my way again."{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=January 24, 2024 |title=How the 2023 Rams helped Sean McVay rediscover his way |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39370767/los-angeles-rams-coach-sean-mcvay-2023-rejuvenated |access-date=January 28, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ====2024 season==== {{See also|2024 Los Angeles Rams season}} In 2024, McVay entered his eighth season as head coach of the Rams, reinvigorated after considering retirement during the previous offseason. Despite McVay's renewed enthusiasm, the Rams faced difficulties early in the season, starting with a 1–4 record by mid-October. Their sole victory came in Week 3, a 27–24 victory over the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. However, the team struggled with consistency, particularly on defense, but McVay remained optimistic about the development of younger players, emphasizing that the 2024 season felt like "Year 1 again" as the team transitioned into a new era. Following the bye week, the Rams earned back-to-back home wins against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] (20–15) in Week 7 and [[Minnesota Vikings]] (30–20) in Week 8. With the latter, McVay became Rams franchise all-time leader in overall coaching victories with 80, surpassing the total of 79 by [[John Robinson (American football coach)|John Robinson]], who coached the Rams from 1983 to 1991. In Week 13, McVay surpassed Robinson for most regular season victories in team history with his 76th coming in a 21–14 victory over the [[New Orleans Saints]]. Four weeks later, a 19–9 win over the [[New York Jets]] clinched for McVay his seventh winning season in eight years, and the following week the Rams defeated the [[Arizona Cardinals]] 13–9.{{Cite web |title=2024 Los Angeles Rams Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/ram/2024.htm |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} The Rams' 10th victory of the season, combined with a strength of victory tiebreaker, clinched the [[NFC West]] division title for the fourth time in eight years under McVay, as well as advancing to the playoffs for the sixth time in McVay's eight seasons{{cite web | last=DaSilva | first=Cameron | title=Rams clinch NFC West thanks to Commanders' win over Falcons in overtime | website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-12-29 | url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2024/12/29/nfl-playoffs-rams-clinch-nfc-west-teams-win/ | access-date=2025-01-22}} Preparations to host the [[2024 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] in an NFC Wild Card Game were disrupted by the outbreak of the [[January 2025 Southern California wildfires]]. Initially maintaining a normal practice schedule as a series of fires broke out in surrounding communities, the [[NFL]] decided (along with the concurrence of both franchises) to move the game to [[State Farm Stadium]] in [[Glendale, Arizona]]. Despite the difficulties, McVay was able to keep his team focused and ready to play. The result was a resounding 27–9 rout of the Vikings that advanced the Rams to the divisional round. Following the triumph, McVay praised his team staying resilient amid all the adversity and becoming an inspiration for their stricken community. "With everything that's going on with our community, everything that these guys have gone through, I thought they epitomized and they represented the city the right way. You talk about sports offering a platform for people to come together, offer a little bit of temporary relief, and I thought the way that our team competed tonight was what it looked like."{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Wyatt |date=January 19, 2025 |title=From the Podium: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford discuss defense, offense dominance in wild card win |url=https://www.therams.com/news/from-the-podium-sean-mcvay-matthew-stafford-discuss-defense-offense-dominance-in-wild-card-win-vikings-nine-sacks |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=TheRams.com |language=en}} Against [[2024 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia]] in an NFC Divisional Playoff game, the Rams stayed close through three quarters, but critical turnovers and miscues had the Rams down late before mounting a comeback that fell short in the final minute. After the game, McVay again was effusive in praise for his team despite the losing effort. McVay stated: "I love this group, I love this coaching staff, I love these players, and I also understand and appreciate how difficult it is to be in positions like this where you've got the game in hand. I feel like we had total control toward the latter part of that game. Momentum was in our favor and we had an opportunity to win that game, and we just came up short."{{Cite web |last=Boston |first=Freddie |date=January 19, 2025 |title=Sean McVay delivers an emotional message after Rams' heartbreaking loss |url=https://ramblinfan.com/sean-mcvay-delivers-emotional-message-after-rams-heartbreaking-loss |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Ramblin' Fan|publisher=USA Today |language=en}} ====2025 season==== {{See also|2025 Los Angeles Rams season}} [[file:2025 Titans vs Rams - Rams Sideline 2-13 screenshot.png|thumb|right|McVay (center) coaching the Rams in 2025]] Coming off an [[NFC West]] title, the Rams now entered McVay's ninth season as a top contender to reach [[Super Bowl LX]], and early wins over Houston (14–9) and Tennessee (33–19) seemed to confirm expectations. But in Week 3, the Rams had built a 26–7 third quarter lead on the road against the [[2025 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] before the defending world champions rallied to score 26 unanswered points, including two blocked field goal attempts on the Rams' final two possessions (the second one was returned for the game-sealing touchdown) dooming their chances in a 33–26 loss. McVay took responsibility for himself and his coaching staff for the playcalling in the second half that led the way to Los Angeles's first defeat of the season, saying, "We came in with the expectations of being aggressive, playing to be able to win the football game. I thought that was reflected in how we did it. I'll always be critical of, am I putting players in the most successful outcomes and are we collectively as a staff?"{{Cite web |last=Vierra |first=Brock |date=September 23, 2025 |title=Sean McVay Gets Candid About Decisions Made in Rams' Loss |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/rams/onsi/sean-mcvay-nick-sirianni-los-angeles-matthew-stafford-philadelphia-eagles |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=SI.com}} The Rams bounced back with a wild 27–20 victory against the then-unbeaten [[2025 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 4, but four days later on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'', Los Angeles came out flat in falling behind 14–0 to visiting [[2025 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco]], and though the Rams rallied to force overtime, again special teams miscues and a critical fumble by running back [[Kyren Williams]] at the goal line prevented Los Angeles from taking the lead. In the extra period following a 49ers field goal, the Rams drove to the San Francisco 11-yard line where on fourth-and-1, Williams was stuffed for no gain. McVay quickly blamed himself for the play call, lamenting in his postgame press conference, "I’m sick right now because I put our players in a s----y spot. I’ve got to live with that."{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=October 2, 2025 |title='I'm sick right now': What Sean McVay said after Rams' stunning OT loss to 49ers |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/rams/2025/10/02/rams-sean-mcvay-49ers-quote-overtime-fourth-down/86490980007/ |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today}} The Rams then proceeded to win their next six games. A 42–26 win in a Week 10 rematch at San Francisco made McVay the Rams' franchise leader in total games coached (154) and Los Angeles's 31–28 loss at [[2025 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina]] in Week 13 to end the streak gave him the most regular season games coached (144). Prior to a 45–17 win at [[2025 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona]] in Week 14, McVay fell ill and traveled separately from the team.{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2025 |title=Rams' Sean McVay to coach Sunday despite illness |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/rams-sean-mcvay-coach-sunday-despite-illness--flm-2025-12-07/ |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=Reuters.com}} A 41–34 triumph at home in Week 15 versus [[2025 Detroit Lions season|Detroit]] secured for McVay his franchise-best seventh playoff berth as head coach,{{Cite web |last=Stretton |first=Max |date=December 15, 2025 |title=Rams Beat Lions 41–34 to Clinch Playoff Berth |url=https://lamag.com/sports/rams-beat-lions-41-34-to-clinch-playoff-berth/ |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=LAMag.com}} and the next day, McVay and his wife welcomed the birth of their second son Christian, with McVay quipping that he had not gotten much sleep in the runup to the delivery. "What a crazy week to be playing on a Thursday...This is a good challenge. But it's a blessing to be able to play in meaningful games this late in the season. And so I've got a lot of appreciation for our staff. And fighting a good fight right now."{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=December 16, 2025 |title=Rams HC Sean McVay announces birth of son, Christian |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47325967/los-angeles-rams-sean-mcvay-son-birth |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=ESPN.com}} But back-to-back losses at [[2025 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle]] in Week 16 (38–37 in overtime on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'') and at [[2025 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta]] in Week 17 (27–24 on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'') knocked the Rams out of contention for their second straight division crown.{{Cite web |last=Cwik |first=Chris |date=December 30, 2025 |title=Sean McVay says Rams won't rest starters in Week 18 despite being out of NFC West race: 'We need to play better' |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/article/sean-mcvay-says-rams-wont-rest-starters-in-week-18-despite-being-out-of-nfc-west-race-we-need-to-play-better-135316036.html |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=Sports.Yahoo.com |language=en}} Following the loss to Seattle, McVay fired special teams coordinator [[Chase Blackburn]], the first in-season dismissal of McVay's career.{{Cite web |last=Grosbard |first=Adam |date=December 22, 2025 |title=Why now was time for Rams' Sean McVay to make first in-season coaching change |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2025/12/22/why-now-was-time-for-rams-sean-mcvay-to-make-first-in-season-coaching-change/ |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=OCRegister.com |language=en}} The Rams played their starters in a 37–20 victory over Arizona in Week 18 to finish the regular season with a 12–5 record, with McVay's 100th win (regular season and postseason) helping to match the second-highest single season win total of his career. McVay was pleased with his team's effort and eager to get on to the postseason and a rematch with [[NFC South]] champion Carolina, saying, "I'm proud of the group and now we move forward. It’s a cool opportunity to be able to earn a chance to be one of the 14 teams in this tournament. I know how difficult it is and how competitive this league is. And to go back to a place that...This team humbled us a handful of weeks ago. And so, what a great challenge. As a competitor, if this doesn't get you excited, then I don't know what the hell you're doing."{{Cite web |last=Vierra |first=Brock |date=January 4, 2026 |title=Rams Sean McVay Reflects on Win Over Cardinals |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/rams/onsi/los-angeles-sean-mcvay-reflects-win-over-cardinals |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=SI.com}} Playing on the road against the Panthers in an NFC Wild Card Game, Los Angeles charged out to a 14–0 lead, fell behind late but rallied for a 34–31 victory. Traveling for the NFC Divisional Round, numerous media outlets pointed out the unusual fact that with his team taking on the [[2025 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], McVay would be facing the 15th different playoff team in 15 career playoff games up to that point.{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |date=January 12, 2026 |title=Sean McVay will coach 15th postseason game — against 15th different opponent |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/sean-mcvay-will-coach-15th-postseason-game-against-15th-different-opponent |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=NBCSports.com}} Playing in front of a national TV audience on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'', the Rams battled the Bears in the snow and wind to a 20–17 overtime victory. While elated with the win, McVay was very self-critical of his own preparation and strategy, saying after the game, "I did not like the feel for the flow of the game that I had outside of the first series where our guys did a great job...Defensively, it kept us in it, in spite of how poor of a job I did for our group. But like I said, you know, I'm really grateful for this group, being able to find a way, stick with it, and be able to overcome some bad coaching by me tonight."{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=January 19, 2026 |title=Sean McVay, Rams advance to NFC Championship Game after Bears' rally falls short |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/sean-mcvay-rams-advance-to-nfc-championship-game-after-bears-rally-falls-short |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=NFL.com}} The day before coaching in his third conference championship, McVay celebrated his 40th birthday, joking at a press conference that week, "I'm not a big birthday guy...And if you guys say, 'Happy 40th,' I'll slap the (expletive) out of you."{{Cite web |last=Beacham |first=Greg |date=January 23, 2026 |title=Sean McVay turns 40 with a new perspective on football and the same dreams for his Los Angeles Rams |url=https://apnews.com/article/rams-seahawks-nfc-championship-mcvay-bebb60498cb2797ceaddf703a68c3744 |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=APNews.com}} In the [[NFC Championship Game]], the Rams rematched with NFC West rival Seattle and fought a close battle through four quarters before falling 31–27 to the Seahawks. It was McVay's first loss when playing for a conference title after previous wins in [[2018 Los Angeles Rams season|2018]] and [[2021 Los Angeles Rams season|2021]]. McVay appeared stunned in front of the press following the game. "We came here with the expectation to win. We had our chances. They made their plays," McVay told reporters. "It was a great back-and-forth game by two great teams, but a couple critical errors ended up costing us. Love this team. It's one of my all-time favorites. I'll be honest with you guys right now, I'm pretty numb."{{Cite web |last=Sandoval |first=Curt |date=January 25, 2026 |title=Rams head coach Sean McVay, players react after emotional loss |url=https://abc7.com/live-updates/rams-face-seahawks-seattle-trip-super-bowl-line/18471368/entry/18475442/ |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=ABC7.com}} Just over a week after the end of the Rams' season, the team announced that McVay along with general manager [[Les Snead]] had both signed contract extensions to remain in their respective positions, though length and terms were unspecified. In a statement announcing the extensions, Rams owner [[Stan Kroenke]] lavished praise on McVay and Snead, saying, "As we enter their 10th season together, it is only fitting to reflect on the tremendous success Sean and Les have brought to this franchise, and the indelible impact they have made on Los Angeles and the NFL...and we are thrilled they will be leading the Los Angeles Rams for years to come." Speaking at his season-ending press conference following the announcement of his contract extension, McVay thanked the Kroenke family for their unwavering loyalty and confidence in him. "I've felt the most supported in the moments that you need it the most. And it's been unconditional, and it's been consistent, and our relationship is only built over these...going into year 10. And I value that more than, I think, ever before."{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=February 2, 2026 |title=Rams sign coach Sean McVay, GM Les Snead to multiyear extensions |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47807493/rams-sign-coach-sean-mcvay-gm-les-snead-multiyear-extensions |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=ESPN.com}} ==Head coaching record== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size: 95%; text-align:center;" |- ! rowspan="2"|Team !! rowspan="2"|Year !! colspan="5"|Regular season !! colspan="4"|Postseason |- !
