{{Short description|Australian actress and theatre director (born 1985)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=February 2014}} {{Use Australian English|date=February 2014}} {{Infobox person | name = Shari Sebbens | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1985|4|22 |df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Darwin, Northern Territory|Darwin]], [[Northern Territory]] Australia | occupation = Actress | known_for = ''[[The Sapphires (film)|The Sapphires]]'' (2012)
''[[Redfern Now]]'' (2012) | years_active = 2010–present | education = [[Darwin High School]] (2001)
[[Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts]]
[[National Institute of Dramatic Art]] ([[Bachelor of Fine Arts|BFA]]) (2009) | family = [[Mitch Torres]] (cousin) }} '''Shari Sebbens''' is an [[Aboriginal Australian]] actress and [[stage director]], known for her debut film role in ''[[The Sapphires (film)|The Sapphires]]'' (2012), as well as many stage and television performances. ==Early life and education== Sebbens, one of six children, was born and raised in [[Darwin, Northern Territory|Darwin]], [[Northern Territory]], Australia.{{cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/movies/dream-time-to-act-out-20120714-222ab.html |title=Dream time to act out |last=Blake|first=Elissa|work=[[Sydney Morning Herald]] |accessdate=8 April 2013|date=15 July 2012}} Her father is a former long-distance coach driver from [[Sydney]] of English descent and her mother, Annarella,{{cite news |url=http://www.ntnews.com.au/article/2013/04/09/319390_entertainment.html |title=Logie double in top night for Top End |last=Palin|first=Megan|work=[[Northern Territory News]]|accessdate=10 April 2013|date=9 April 2013}} an [[Aboriginal Australian|Aboriginal]] education worker from [[Broome, Western Australia]] is of [[Jabirr Jabirr]] and [[Bardi people|Bardi]] heritage.{{cite news | title=Shari Sebbens shines with best of both worlds |date=26 August 2012 | work=[[Herald Sun]] |url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/news/national/shari-sebbens-shines-with-best-of-both-worlds/story-fndo317g-1226458125374 |first=Jonathan |last=Moran | accessdate=8 April 2013}} Sebbens refers to Australian music composer and playwright [[Jimmy Chi]] as her uncle, although they are not related by blood. She is the cousin of writer and film director [[Mitch Torres]]. As a child, Sebbens wanted to become a [[palaeontologist]] or an [[astronaut]] but at the age of thirteen she saw [[Indigenous Australian|Indigenous]] actress (and future ''[[The Sapphires (film)|The Sapphires]]'' co-star) [[Deborah Mailman]] in the film ''[[Radiance (1998 film)|Radiance]]'' (1998) and was inspired to pursue acting. Sebbens graduated from [[Darwin High School]] in 2001{{cite web|title= NamesDatabase: Shari Sebbens|publisher= [[Names Database]]|url= http://namesdatabase.com/people/SEBBENS/SHARI/17445819|accessdate= 5 April 2013|url-status= dead|archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20131002151245/http://namesdatabase.com/people/SEBBENS/SHARI/17445819|archivedate= 2 October 2013|df= dmy-all}} and after two and a half years at [[Nhulunbuy]],{{cite web | last=Steer | first=Adam | title=Shari Sebbens still a 'Darwin girl' | website=Australian Broadcasting Corporation | date=22 April 2013 | url=https://www.abc.net.au/local/stories/2013/04/22/3742199.htm | access-date=27 June 2021}} at age 19, was chosen to participate in "SPARK", a theatre mentorship programme established by the [[Australia Council for the Arts]].{{cite web|title= Characters – Refern Now: Julie|publisher= [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]|url=http://www.abc.net.au/tv/redfernnow/characters/julie.htm|accessdate=5 April 2013}} At 20 she was accepted into the [[Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts]] (WAAPA) where she completed a one-year course in Aboriginal Theatre. Upon completing her studies at WAAPA, Sebbens successfully auditioned for a place at the [[National Institute of Dramatic Art]] (NIDA) in [[Sydney]], where she studied acting full-time for three years,{{cite web|title= The Sapphires Press Kit: About Shari Sebbens|website= Australia at Cannes 2012 ([[Screen Australia]])|url=http://www.australiaatcannes.com/pdf/Press-Kit_Sapphires.pdf| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202230625/http://www.australiaatcannes.com/pdf/Press-Kit_Sapphires.pdf| archive-date=2 Dec 2013|accessdate=5 April 2013}} graduating in 2009. ==Acting and directing== ===Screen=== Sebbens played Anna in a short film called ''Violet'' in 2010.{{cite news |title=Sydney Theatre Awards 2012 nominations |date=12 December 2012 |work=[[Time Out Sydney]] |url=http://www.au.timeout.com/sydney/theatre/features/11678/sydney-theatre-awards-2012-nominations |first=Darryn |last=King |accessdate=8 April 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121221190244/http://www.au.timeout.com/sydney/theatre/features/11678/sydney-theatre-awards-2012-nominations |archivedate=21 December 2012 |df=dmy-all }} By May 2012, she landed a role in ''[[Redfern Now]]'', a television series about "six inner city households whose lives are changed by a seemingly insignificant incident".{{cite news | title=Cameras Roll on Redfern Now |date=28 May 2012 |publisher=[[TV Tonight]]| url=http://www.tvtonight.com.au/2012/05/cameras-roll-on-redfern-now.html |first=David |last=Knox | accessdate=8 April 2013}}{{cite news|url=http://www.theage.com.au/entertainment/box-seat/redfern-now-back-for-second-series-20121113-299i3.html |title=Redfern Now back for second series |date =13 November 2012 |first=Karl |last=Quinn }} Sebbens secured a role in ''[[The Sapphires (film)|The Sapphires]]'' (2012), a film based on the [[The Sapphires (play)|stage show]] of the same name, written by [[Tony Briggs]]. It was directed by [[Wayne Blair (director)|Wayne Blair]] and also starred [[Deborah Mailman]], [[Jessica Mauboy]], and [[Miranda Tapsell]] (who also co-wrote the script). Sebbens played the role of Kay McCrae, one of four [[Indigenous Australian]] singers "who travel from a mission in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] to [[Vietnam]] to sing for American troops".{{cite news|last=Hohenboken|first=Angus|url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/entertainment/the-sapphires-starring-jessica-mauboy-and-deborah-mailman-is-a-gem-insist-cannes-critics/story-e6frewyr-1226361638562|title=The Sapphires starring Jessica Mauboy and Deborah Mailman is a gem, insist Cannes critics|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=21 May 2012|accessdate=15 June 2012}}{{cite news|last=Moran |first=Jonathon |title=Mauboy's new tilt at movies |url=http://www.ntnews.com.au/article/2011/06/19/241641_entertainment.html |work=[[Northern Territory News]] |date=19 June 2011 |accessdate=25 June 2011}} The cast attended the film's premiere at the [[2012 Cannes Film Festival|65th Annual Cannes Film Festival]] in [[Cannes]], France, on 20 May 2012. '''Jessica Elise De Gouw''' (born February 15, 1988) is an Australian actress. She is known for her role as [[Huntress (Helena Bertinelli)|Helena Bertinelli/The Huntress]] in the television series ''[[Arrow (TV series)|Arrow]]'', as [[Mina Harker|Mina Murray]] and [[Justina Szilágyi|Ilona]] in the [[NBC]] TV series ''[[Dracula (2013 TV series)|Dracula]]'', and as Elizabeth Hawkes in the [[WGN America|WGN]] series ''[[Underground (TV series)|Underground]]''.

==Early life==
De Gouw grew up in [[Lesmurdie, Western Australia|Lesmurdie]], an eastern suburb of [[Perth, Western Australia]], where she attended [[Lesmurdie Senior High School]].<ref name=ynz2012>{{cite web |url=http://nz.news.yahoo.com/a/-/archive/12599452/gouw-set-wow/ |title=De Gouw set to wow in US |date=14 January 2012 |publisher=[[Yahoo! News|Yahoo! New Zealand News]] |access-date=1 March 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130905081739/http://nz.news.yahoo.com/a/-/archive/12599452/gouw-set-wow/ |archive-date=5 September 2013 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> She appeared in an episode of ''[[The Sleepover Club (TV series)|The Sleepover Club]]'', as well as a short film. In 2010, she graduated from [[Curtin University]] with a degree in performance studies. She also appeared in another short film the same year.<ref name="perthnow">{{cite web |url=http://www.perthnow.com.au/news/western-australia/perth-actor-jessice-de-gouw-aiming-at-sci-fi-glory/story-e6frg13u-1226500000489 |title=Perth actor Jessica De Gouw aiming at sci-fi glory |last=Symonds |first=Kristy |date=20 October 2012 |publisher=Perth Now |access-date=1 March 2013}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduation, De Gouw moved to Sydney for her acting career. While there, she appeared in a number of TV series, mainly in guest starring roles.

In 2012, she debuted in the film ''[[Kath & Kimderella]]'' as Isabella, Kath and Kim's maid. She moved to [[Los Angeles]] later that year and landed the recurring role of [[Huntress (Helena Bertinelli)|Helena Bertinelli/The Huntress]] in the action-adventure series, ''[[Arrow (TV series)|Arrow]]''.

In 2013, De Gouw was cast in the [[NBC]] series ''[[Dracula (2013 TV series)|Dracula]]'' as [[Mina Harker|Mina Murray]] alongside [[Jonathan Rhys Meyers]]<ref name="perthnow" /> and [[Oliver Jackson-Cohen]]. The series was cancelled after the first season.

In 2016, De Gouw was cast as fictional [[Abolitionism|abolitionist]] Elizabeth Hawkes in the WGN series, ''[[Underground (TV series)|Underground]]''. She played the lead role Ren Amari in the 2017 feature film ''[[OtherLife]]'' based on the novel ''Solitaire'' by [[Kelley Eskridge]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://kelleyeskridge.com/tag/ben-c-lucas/ |title=OtherLife world premiere |date=19 May 2017 |publisher=[[Kelley Eskridge]] |access-date=17 July 2017}}</ref>

De Gouw appeared in the 2018 Australian television movie ''Riot'', about the 78ers, the Australian LGBTQ rights movement who fought for decriminalisation, recognition and equality.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Inside Alycia Debnam-Carey's Beauty Routine - Grazia|url=https://graziamagazine.com/us/articles/alycia-debnam-carey-interview/|access-date=2021-08-31|website=Grazia USA|date=6 July 2021 |language=en-US}}</ref>

She played the role of Sergeant Klintoff's wife, Louisa, in [[Leah Purcell]]'s debut feature film, ''[[The Drover's Wife (film)|The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson]]'' (2021).

On 11 July 2024, De Gouw was named for Stan Australia series ''[[Sunny Nights]].''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Know |first=David |date=2024-07-11 |title=Production begins on new Stan comedy-drama Sunny Nights {{!}} TV Tonight |url=https://tvtonight.com.au/2024/07/production-begins-on-new-stan-comedy-drama-sunny-nights.html |access-date=2024-07-11 |website=tvtonight.com.au |language=en-AU}}</ref> On 31 January 2025 De Gouw was named as part of the cast for Netflix series ''The Survivors.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knox |first=David |date=2025-01-31 |title=Cast announced for The Survivors {{!}} TV Tonight |url=https://tvtonight.com.au/2025/01/cast-announced-for-the-survivors.html |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=tvtonight.com.au |language=en-AU}}</ref>

==Personal life==
De Gouw was in a relationship for several years with her ''Dracula'' costar, [[Oliver Jackson-Cohen]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Who Is Oliver Jackson-Cohen's Girlfriend? What You Need To Know About Partner Jessica De Gouw |website=[[Capital (radio network)|Capital FM]] |date=8 October 2020 |url=https://www.capitalfm.com/news/celebrity/oliver-jackson-cohen-girlfriend-partner-jessica-de-gouw/ |access-date=31 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014130842/https://www.capitalfm.com/news/celebrity/oliver-jackson-cohen-girlfriend-partner-jessica-de-gouw/ |archive-date=14 October 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In a June 2022 interview, she described herself as [[queer]] and said that she was in a relationship with a woman.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dow |first=Steve |date=3 July 2022 |title='Twitter is the worst!': Actor Jessica de Gouw on being in the public eye |work=The Age |url=https://www.smh.com.au/culture/tv-and-radio/twitter-is-the-worst-actor-jessica-de-gouw-on-being-in-the-public-eye-20220627-p5awz4.html |access-date=18 August 2022}}</ref> De Gouw and her girlfriend, hairstylist Sophie Roberts, spoke about the pair's relationship for the February edition of ''[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]]'' in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Xidias|first=Angelica|date=9 February 2023|title=Sophie Roberts and Jessica De Gouw pen their love story|url=https://www.vogue.com.au/culture/pride/sophie-roberts-jessica-de-gouw/news-story/c6628f9ba93c805f5b49e460d6557d00|access-date=28 March 2023}}</ref>

'''Luis Carlos Ruiz Morales''' (born 8 January 1987) is a Colombian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]].

==Career==
Ruiz was the joint top goal scorer during the [[2013 Categoría Primera A season#Torneo Finalización|2013 Torneo Finalización]] with [[Dayro Moreno]], both scoring 16 goals.

In December 2013, Ruiz claimed he had signed a Four-year contract with [[Neftchi Baku PFK|Neftchi Baku]] in the [[Azerbaijan Premier League|Azerbaijani Premier League]], though this claim was denied by Neftchi.<ref>{{cite web|title=Новичок Нефтчи объявил о своем переходе (ФОТО)|url=http://azerisport.com/football/20131231123124586.html|publisher=azerisport.com|accessdate=30 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title="Görünür, Azərbaycanda "Neftçi"dən başqa klub tanımadığından, "Neftçi"yə gələcəyini düşünür"|url=http://korner.az/v2/xeber/15324/|publisher=korner.az|accessdate=31 December 2013|language=Azerbaijani|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102162934/http://korner.az/v2/xeber/15324/|archive-date=2 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 4 January 2014, Ruiz announced that he wouldn't be joining Neftchi after all and that the statement posted had been the result of hackers hacking his Twitter account.<ref>{{cite web|title=.... will not go to Neftchi.|url=https://twitter.com/RuizEterno27/status/419458206960582656|publisher=[[Twitter]]|accessdate=4 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Luis Karlos Ruis Neftçi barədə açıqlamalarını təkzib etdi|url=http://www.azerisport.com/az/futbol/20140105020433056.html|publisher=azerisport.com|accessdate=4 January 2014|language=Azerbaijani}}</ref>

In February 2014, Ruiz joined [[Shanghai Greenland Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Greenland Shenhua]] in the [[Chinese Super League]]. The transfer fee was about €3 million,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.futbolred.com/liga-postobon/noticias/fecha8apertura2014/luis-carlos-ruiz-se-va-al-futbol-de-china/13565387|website=Futbolred.com |language=Spanish |title=Luis Carlos Ruiz se va al fútbol de China}}</ref> and he linked up with fellow Colombian [[Giovanni Moreno]]. In June 2014, Ruiz returned to Colombia, signing for [[Atlético Nacional]].

'''Tarik Daniel Skubal''' (born November 20, 1996) is an American professional [[baseball]] [[pitcher]] for the [[Los Angeles Dodgers]] of [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB). He has previously played in MLB for the [[Detroit Tigers]]. Skubal was selected by the Tigers in the ninth round of the [[2018 MLB draft]] and made his MLB debut in 2020. 

Skubal is a two-time [[American League]] (AL) [[Cy Young Award]] winner (2024 and 2025). In 2024, Skubal was named an [[Major League Baseball All-Star Game|All-Star]] and became the first American League pitcher since 2011 to capture both the pitching [[Triple Crown (baseball)|Triple Crown]] and the Cy Young Award in a full season. He was again named an All-Star in 2025 and won his second consecutive Cy Young Award.

==Early life==
Skubal was born in [[Hayward, California]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Beck | first=Jason | title=Tarik Skubal reflects on time spent at the Coliseum | website=MLB.com | date=2024-09-06 | url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-reflects-on-time-spent-at-the-coliseum | access-date=2025-11-19}}</ref> His father is an elementary school teacher and retired coach.<ref name="o052">{{cite web |last=Henning |first=Lynn |date=March 5, 2020 |title=Among Tigers' batch of budding stars, Tarik Skubal could end up shining brightest |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2020/03/04/skubals-future-could-possibly-detroit-tigers-future/4960307002/ |access-date=August 24, 2024 |website=Detroit News}}</ref> He has three brothers and one stepbrother.<ref name="n664">{{cite web | last=Seidel | first=Jeff | title=Why is Detroit Tigers' Tarik Skubal so competitive? Dad knows | website=Detroit Free Press | date=April 21, 2020 | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/columnists/jeff-seidel/2020/04/21/detroit-tigers-tarik-skubal-so-competitive-father-knows/5132690002/ | access-date=August 24, 2024}}</ref> He is of paternal [[Czechs|Czech]] descent.<ref name="SN">{{cite web |last1=Heyen |first1=Billy |title=Tarik Skubal's nationality, name meaning tell cool story of Tigers' ace pitcher |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/mlb/detroit-tigers/news/tarik-skubal-nationality-name-meaning-tigers-ace-pitcher/c591f810210271ce8f493562?utm_source=yahoo&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=appeared_on |website=Sporting News |publisher=Sporting News Holdings |access-date=5 May 2026}}</ref> His name Tarik means "striker" in [[Arabic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-30 |title=Tarik Skubal's nationality, name meaning tell cool story of Tigers' ace pitcher {{!}} Sporting News |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/mlb/detroit-tigers/news/tarik-skubal-nationality-name-meaning-tigers-ace-pitcher/c591f810210271ce8f493562 |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=www.sportingnews.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

Skubal grew up a fan of the [[Oakland Athletics]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Varnes|first=Charlotte|title=Tigers ace, Bay native Skubal, on pitching in Oakland one last time: 'A team should be here'|website=San Francisco Chronicle|date=September 7, 2024|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/athletics/article/tigers-ace-bay-native-skubal-a-s-exit-a-19749659.php|access-date=July 30, 2025}}</ref> He played two years of [[Little League Baseball]], representing [[Cordelia, California]], and the wider [[Tri-Valley]] area.<ref name=":1">{{cite news |last1=Keown |first1=Tim |date=July 9, 2025 |title=The extraordinary mystery of the Tigers' Tarik Skubal |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/45695708/detroit-tigers-tarik-skubal-cy-young-pitcher-mlb-all-star-game-2025 |access-date=July 10, 2025 |work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> After his family moved to [[Kingman, Arizona]], he attended the [[Kingman Academy of Learning]].<ref name=rise/>

Skubal enrolled at [[Seattle University]] to play [[college baseball]] for the [[Seattle Redhawks baseball|Seattle Redhawks]]; it was the only [[NCAA Division I]] school to offer him a scholarship.<ref name=rise>{{Cite web|last=Stavenhagen|first=Cody|date=February 20, 2020|title=The rise of Tarik Skubal|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1623070/2020/02/20/the-rise-of-tarik-skubal/|access-date=June 20, 2021|website=The Athletic}}</ref> In 2015, Skubal was recognized as a Collegiate Baseball Freshman All-American. Following this season, Skubal missed most of the 2016 season and all of 2017 after undergoing [[Tommy John surgery]]. Despite the injury, he was drafted by the [[Arizona Diamondbacks]] in the 29th round of the [[2017 Major League Baseball draft]]. He did not sign, opting instead to return to Seattle.<ref name="u956">{{cite web | last=Bearden | first=Beau | title=Life throws Skubal a curveball, but Academy grad makes the best of it | website=Kingman Daily Miner | date=April 24, 2024 | url=https://www.kdminer.com/life-throws-skubal-a-curveball-but-academy-grad-makes-the-best-of-it/article_6894b8e2-e172-5e64-a21e-133571cc3f31.html | access-date=August 24, 2024}}</ref> Skubal had a combined 21–7 record as a starter for the Redhawks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tarik Skubal - Baseball Stats - The Baseball Cube |url=https://www.thebaseballcube.com/content/player/195562/#:~:text=Player%20page%20for%20Tarik%20Skubal%20of%20the%20Detroit |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=TheBaseballCube.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2018, he led the team with 106 strikeouts and 56 walks, pitching 80 innings in his final season in Seattle.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 Seattle Redhawks - The Baseball Cube |url=https://www.thebaseballcube.com/content/stats/college~2018~21265/ |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=TheBaseballCube.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Detroit Tigers===
====Early career====
The [[Detroit Tigers]] selected Skubal in the ninth round with the 255th overall selection of the [[2018 MLB draft]].<ref name="p131">{{cite web | last=Bearden | first=Beau | title=Kingman Academy grad Skubal drafted in ninth round of MLB Draft | website=Kingman Daily Miner | date=April 24, 2024 | url=https://www.kdminer.com/kingman-academy-grad-skubal-drafted-in-ninth-round-of-mlb-draft/article_f5a1b801-f48b-530f-91e2-608a1a082bdd.html | access-date=August 24, 2024}}</ref><ref name="d204">{{cite web | last=Bearden | first=Beau | title=Skubal taking the next step in his baseball journey | website=Kingman Daily Miner | date=April 24, 2024 | url=https://www.kdminer.com/skubal-taking-the-next-step-in-his-baseball-journey/article_a61481b2-cc84-561c-947c-bf9c73fdb567.html | access-date=August 24, 2024}}</ref> He received a $350,000 [[Signing bonus|bonus]] for signing a contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tarik Skubal - Stats - Pitching |url=https://www.fangraphs.com/players/tarik-skubal/22267/stats?position=P |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=FanGraphs Baseball |language=en}}</ref> After the draft, Skubal spent his first professional season with the [[Gulf Coast Tigers]], [[Connecticut Tigers]], and [[West Michigan Whitecaps]], pitching to a combined 3–0 record and 0.40 [[earned run average]] (ERA) in {{frac|22|1|3}} innings pitched.<ref name="k014">{{Cite web |last=Eddy |first=Dave |date=February 13, 2019 |title=5 Prospects Who Should Have Made the Detroit Tigers Top 50 |url=https://www.prospects1500.com/al-central/tigers/5-prospects-who-should-have-made-the-detroit-tigers-top-50/ |access-date=August 24, 2024 |website=Prospects1500.com}}</ref> He started 2019 with the [[Lakeland Flying Tigers]].<ref name="k030">{{cite web | last=Seidel | first=Jeff | title=Detroit Tigers' Tarik Skubal could be the steal of 2018 draft | website=Detroit Free Press | date=May 7, 2019 | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/columnists/jeff-seidel/2019/05/07/detroit-tigers-prospect-tarik-skubal/1123438001/ | access-date=August 24, 2024}}</ref> He earned a [[Call-up (baseball)|call-up]] to the [[Erie SeaWolves]] on July 5. Over his first three starts with Erie, he had a 0.56 ERA with 34 strikeouts, giving up five hits in 16 innings. His performances over the season raised his ranking in MLB.com's 2019 Prospect Watch from a preseason #20 ranking in the Tigers' organization to a #4 spot at the midseason update on July 27.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/milb/prospects/2019|title=MLB.com 2019 Prospect Watch|website=Major League Baseball|language=en-US|access-date=July 27, 2019}}</ref> He finished the season at [[Double-A (baseball)|Double-A]] Erie with a 2–3 record, 2.13 ERA, 1.02 WHIP. Opponents hit just .168 off him. Overall in 2019, in [[High-A]] and Double-A, Skubal struck out 179 batters in {{frac|122|2|3}} innings.<ref name=minors>{{cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/register/player.fcgi?id=skubal000tar|title=Tarik Skubal Amateur, College & Minor League Statistics|work=Baseball Reference|access-date=October 14, 2026}}</ref>

The Tigers invited Skubal to spring training in 2020.<ref name="i562">{{cite web | last=Woodbery | first=Evan | title=Tigers' Tarik Skubal makes it look so easy in spring debut | website=mlive | date=February 21, 2020 | url=https://www.mlive.com/tigers/2020/02/tigers-tarik-skubal-makes-it-look-so-easy-in-spring-debut.html | access-date=August 24, 2024}}</ref> On August 18, Skubal was recalled from the Tigers' satellite training facility in Toledo, and he made his MLB debut later that day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beck |first=Jason  |date=August 17, 2020 |title=Tigers call up top prospects Mize, Skubal |url=https://www.mlb.com/tigers/news/casey-mize-tarik-skubal-called-up |access-date=August 19, 2020 |website=MLB.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Beck |first=Jason  |date=August 18, 2020 |title='He just hits': Paredes impresses in debut |url=https://www.mlb.com/tigers/news/isaac-paredes-notches-first-career-hit-rbi |access-date=August 19, 2020 |website=MLB.com}}</ref> On August 29, Skubal earned his first major league win, besting the [[Minnesota Twins]]. In five innings pitched, Skubal allowed two earned runs and three hits while striking out two and walking none in the Tigers' 4–2 win.<ref>{{ cite web | url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tigers-sweep-doubleheader-against-twins | title=Something old, new lead Tigers in DH sweep | work=MLB.com | last=Beck | first=Jason | date=August 29, 2020 | access-date=August 31, 2020 }}</ref> With the [[2020 Detroit Tigers season|2020 Detroit Tigers]], Skubal appeared in 8 games, compiling a 1–4 record with 5.63 ERA and 37 strikeouts in 32 innings pitched.<ref name=":0">{{cite web| url = https://www.mlb.com/player/tarik-skubal-669373| title = Tarik Skubal Stats, Fantasy & News {{!}} Detroit Tigers| website = [[MLB.com]]}}</ref> His [[Cut fastball|cutter]], which averaged {{convert|95.4|mph|kph|abbr=on}}, was the fastest cutter of any major league pitcher in 2020.<ref>[https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/pitch-arsenals?year=2020&min=100&type=avg_speed&hand=&sort=3&sortDir=desc Pitch Arsenals Leaderboard], baseballsavant.mlb.com</ref>

====2021====
On March 24, 2021, new Tigers manager [[A. J. Hinch]] announced that Skubal had made the [[Opening Day]] roster out of spring training and would be in the Tigers' starting rotation.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2021/03/24/detroit-tigers-roster-julio-teheran-tarik-skubal/4796255001/ | title=Julio Teheran, Tarik Skubal make Detroit Tigers' Opening Day roster as starters | website=freep.com | last=Petzold | first=Evan | date=March 24, 2021 | access-date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> On July 3, Skubal recorded his 100th strikeout of the season, becoming the first Tiger rookie ever to strike out at least 100 batters before the [[All-Star break (MLB)|All-Star break]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Day |first=Brandon |date=July 8, 2021 |title=Detroit at Minnesota preview: Hot Tigers look to carry momentum into the All-Star break |url=https://www.blessyouboys.com/2021/7/8/22568078/detroit-at-minnesota-preview-tarik-skubal-j-a-happ |access-date=July 9, 2021 |website=Bless You Boys|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> On August 25, against the [[St. Louis Cardinals]], Skubal recorded strikeouts for the first six outs of the game, finishing with ten strikeouts in five innings of work.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2021/08/25/tarik-skubal-shines-st-louis-cardinals-clip-detroit-tigers-10/5587831001/ |title=Tarik Skubal shines, but Cardinals clip Tigers in 10 innings |publisher=The Detroit News |last=McCosky |first=Chris |date=August 25, 2021 |access-date=August 26, 2021}}</ref> On September 25, Skubal reached 200 career strikeouts in his first 38 appearances, the fewest number of games in Tigers history that a pitcher needed to reach that milestone. Overall in 2021, Skubal pitched in 31 games, starting all but two of them, posting an 8–12 record and 4.34 ERA while striking out 164 batters in {{frac|149|1|3}} innings.<ref name=":0" />

====2022====
Skubal continued to pitch in the Tigers starting rotation in 2022. After posting a 7–8 record with a 3.52 ERA, 111 [[ERA+]], 1.16 WHIP and 117 strikeouts in {{frac|117|2|3}} innings, he was placed on the [[injured list]] on August 3 with fatigue in his pitching arm. On August 17, the Tigers announced Skubal had undergone flexor tendon surgery, definitively ending his 2022 season and likely sidelining him for the beginning of 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/mlb/news/tigers-pitcher-tarik-skubal-undergoes-flexor-tendon-surgery-could-miss-large-portion-of-2023-season/ |title=Tigers pitcher Tarik Skubal undergoes flexor tendon surgery, could miss large portion of 2023 season |website=CBSsports.com |last=Snyder |first=Matt |date=August 17, 2022 |access-date=August 25, 2022}}</ref>

====2023====
On March 14, 2023, the Tigers moved Skubal to the 60-day injured list, stating that he wasn't expected back on the mound until summer.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mlive.com/tigers/2023/03/tigers-claim-pitcher-off-waivers-from-cardinals-tarik-skubal-goes-to-60-day-il.html |title=Tigers claim pitcher off waivers from Cardinals; Tarik Skubal goes to 60-day IL |website=MLive.com |last=Woodbery |first=Evan |date=March 14, 2023 |access-date=March 17, 2023}}</ref> He was activated for his season debut on July 4.<ref name="c128">{{cite web |date=July 4, 2023 |title=Tigers' Tarik Skubal: Activated for season debut |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/tigers-tarik-skubal-activated-for-season-debut/ |access-date=August 24, 2024 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> He was named American League [[Major League Baseball Pitcher of the Month Award|Pitcher of the Month]] in September, finishing his final five starts with a 4–0 record and 0.90 ERA.<ref name="SkubalSepPOM">{{Cite web |last=Beck |first=Jason |date=April 28, 2024 |title=Skubal proves he's 'one of the best' after another gem |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-pitches-seven-innings-of-one-run-ball-in-tigers-win |access-date=May 13, 2024 |website=MLB.com}}</ref>  In 2023, he pitched {{frac|80|1|3}} innings over 15 starts, posting a 7–3 record with a 2.80 ERA and 102 strikeouts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tarik Skubal 2023 Pitching Game Logs |url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/players/gl.fcgi?id=skubata01&t=p&year=2023 |access-date=August 24, 2024 |website=Baseball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He ranked in the top 4 percent of MLB pitchers in 2023 at earning strikeouts and limiting walks, and his expected ERA was in the top 1 percent of pitchers, according to Baseball Savant.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tarik Skubal Stats: Statcast, Visuals & Advanced Metrics |url=https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/savant-player/tarik-skubal-669373?stats=statcast-r-pitching-mlb |access-date=October 7, 2024 |website=Baseball Savant |publisher=MLB.com}}</ref>

====2024: Triple Crown and Cy Young Award====
[[File:Tarik Skubal (53947874625) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Skubal in 2024]]
Skubal started for the Tigers on [[Opening Day]] of the 2024 season, throwing six shutout innings to lead the Tigers to a 1–0 victory over the [[Chicago White Sox]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petzold |first=Evan |date=April 4, 2024 |title=Detroit Tigers' Tarik Skubal hopes to 'get used to' big crowds at home in unexpected start |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2024/04/04/detroit-tigers-tarik-skubal-excited-opening-day-comerica-park/73202674007/ |access-date=2025-04-27 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref><ref name="w955">{{cite web | last=Beck | first=Jason | title=Tarik Skubal logs six scoreless frames in Tigers' Opening Day win over White Sox | website=MLB.com | date=March 29, 2024 | url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-tigers-opening-day-2024 | access-date=August 24, 2024}}</ref> On April 28, Skubal became the first pitcher in Tigers franchise history to strike out 40+ batters through his first six starts with fewer than nine walks (he had 41 strikeouts and only six walks to date).<ref name=SkubalSepPOM/> In a May 5 game against the [[New York Yankees]], Skubal became the first Tigers pitcher in over 100 years to strike out 12 or more batters without issuing a walk. The last Tiger pitcher to do so was [[Eric Erickson (baseball)|Eric Erickson]] (in a 16-inning complete game) on May 24, 1918.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lastwordonsports.com/baseball/2024/05/06/tarik-skubal-tigers-pitcher-history/|title=Tigers Breakout Pitcher Makes Franchise History Against The Yankees|first=Matt|last=Graves|website=lastwordonsports.com|date=May 6, 2024|access-date=May 13, 2024}}</ref>

On July 7, Skubal was selected to represent the Tigers in the [[2024 Major League Baseball All-Star Game|2024 All-Star Game]] being held July 16, along with teammate [[Riley Greene]]. At the time of his selection, Skubal had a 10–3 record, 2.37 ERA, a league-best 0.90 WHIP and 132 strikeouts in 110 innings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCoskey |first=Chris |date=July 7, 2024 |title=Tigers' Riley Greene, Tarik Skubal selected to play in MLB's All-Star Game |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2024/07/07/detroit-tigers-riley-greene-tarik-skubal-selected-mlb-all-star-game/74320741007/ |access-date=July 9, 2024 |website=Detroit News}}</ref> He pitched a 1-2-3 second inning in the All-Star Game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/gameday/nl-all-stars-vs-al-all-stars/2024/07/16/747298/final/box|title=NL All-Stars vs. AL All-Stars - Final Box|work=mlb.com|date=July 16, 2024|access-date=July 18, 2024}}</ref>

Skubal finished the season with 18 wins (18–4 record), a 2.39 ERA, 0.922 WHIP, and 228 strikeouts. He became the first pitcher to win the [[Triple Crown (baseball)|Triple Crown]] since [[Shane Bieber]] in the [[COVID-19]] shortened [[2020 Major League Baseball season|2020 season]]. He and fellow Cy Young awardee [[Chris Sale]] were the first pitchers to earn the Triple Crown in a full season since [[2011 Major League Baseball season|2011]], when both [[Justin Verlander]] (AL) and [[Clayton Kershaw]] (NL) earned the distinction.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-wins-2024-american-league-triple-crown |title=Triple Crown! Skubal paces AL in wins, K's and ERA |website=[[MLB.com]] |first=Brent |last=Maguire |date=September 29, 2024 |access-date=September 29, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Paul |first1=Tony |title='Glad he's on our team': Tigers' Tarik Skubal wraps up AL Triple Crown in pitching |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2024/09/29/detroit-tigers-ace-tarik-skubal-wraps-up-triple-crown/75445972007/ |access-date=September 30, 2024 |work=The Detroit News |date=September 29, 2024}}</ref> Additionally, Skubal led the American League with a 170 ERA+ and 2.50 fielding-independent pitching (FIP) rating, while leading all major league pitchers with a 6.3 Wins Against Replacement (WAR).<ref name=br>{{cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/players/s/skubata01.shtml|title=Tarik Skubal Statistics|work=Baseball Reference|access-date=October 14, 2026}}</ref>

On October 1, Skubal earned the first postseason win of his career after throwing six scoreless innings with six strikeouts against the [[Houston Astros]] in Game 1 of the [[2024 American League Wild Card Series|AL Wild Card Series]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rieken |first=Kristie |date=2024-10-01 |title=Skubal shines in playoff debut to help Detroit Tigers to first playoff win in more than a decade |url=https://apnews.com/article/tigers-skubal-mlb-playoffs-d14112472810b0e36d1be4ca0fb8a268 |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> He threw seven shutout innings against the [[Cleveland Guardians]] in Game 2 of the [[2024 American League Division Series|AL Division Series]], and took the loss in Game 5 after giving up a [[Grand slam (baseball)|grand slam]] in the fifth inning, ultimately losing the series. Across three games and 19.0 innings of the [[2024 Major League Baseball postseason|2024 postseason]], Skubal recorded a 1–1 record with a 2.37 ERA and 20 strikeouts.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Tarik Skubal Career Postseason Stats |url=https://www.statmuse.com/mlb/ask/tarik-skubal-career-postseason-stats |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref>

After the season, Skubal won the [[AL Cy Young|AL Cy Young Award]] for the first time in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Franco |first=Anthony |date=November 20, 2024 |title=Tarik Skubal Wins American League Cy Young Award |url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/11/tarik-skubal-wins-american-league-cy-young-award.html |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=MLB Trade Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref> On the strength of his Triple Crown campaign, he won the Cy Young Award unanimously, earning all 30 first-place votes.<ref>{{cite web|last=Beck |first=Jason |title=Skubal wins AL Cy Young unanimously after Triple Crown campaign |url=https://www.mlb.com/tigers/news/tarik-skubal-2024-al-cy-young-award-winner |website=[[MLB.com]] |date=November 20, 2024 |access-date=November 20, 2024}}</ref>

====2025: All-Star and second Cy Young====
On January 9, 2025, the Tigers and Skubal agreed to a one-year, $10.15 million contract, avoiding arbitration.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rogers |first=Anne |title=Skubal, Tigers agree to $10.15M deal to avoid arbitration |url=https://www.mlb.com/milb/news/tarik-skubal-tigers-2025-contract|website=[[MLB.com]] |date=January 9, 2025 |access-date=January 30, 2025}}</ref> Skubal started for the Tigers on [[Opening Day]] of the season, taking a 5–4 loss against the defending [[World Series]] champion [[Los Angeles Dodgers]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Chen | first=Sonja | title='Teoscar tax' pays off as Hernández, Ohtani come out swinging | website=MLB.com | date=March 27, 2025 | url=https://www.mlb.com/news/teoscar-hernandez-shohei-ohtani-homer-in-dodgers-home-opener | access-date=April 8, 2025}}</ref> On May 25, Skubal pitched a [[Maddux (statistic)|Maddux]], throwing only 94 pitches in a complete-game shutout versus the Guardians, with a career-high-tying 13 strikeouts, no walks, and two hits allowed. The 5–0 victory was both the first complete game and the first shutout of his career.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McCosky |first1=Chris |date=May 25, 2025 |title=Tarik Skubal dominates Guardians with complete-game two-hitter, Tigers win |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2025/05/25/tarik-skubal-dominates-guardians-with-complete-game-two-hitter-tigers-win/83850573007/ |access-date=25 May 2025 |website=The Detroit News}}</ref> 

On June 24, Skubal earned the 50th win of his career after allowing six hits, one walk, and four runs, while striking out eight batters in 6 innings to beat the [[Athletics (baseball)|Athletics]] 11–4.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Beck|first=Jason|title=Skubal settles in, bats take over to make Tigers first to 50 wins|url=https://mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-beats-athletics-as-tigers-reach-50-wins|website=MLB.com|date=June 24, 2025|access-date=June 25, 2025}}</ref> In his next start on June 29, Detroit defeated the Minnesota Twins, 3–0, behind Skubal's seven innings with 13 strikeouts and one hit allowed; each Twins starter struck out at least once. He was the first pitcher in Tigers history with at least 13 strikeouts and one hit or fewer in a game.<ref>{{cite news |last=McCosky |first=Chris |date=June 30, 2025 |title=Tarik Skubal dominates Twins with 13 strikeouts, one hit allowed |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/ |access-date=September 25, 2025 |work=The Detroit News}}</ref><ref name="Romo">{{cite news |last=Romo |first=Christian |date=July 6, 2025 |title=Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal named to his second AL All-Star team |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2025/07/06/tarik-skubal-all-star-game-american-league-detroit-tigers/84457795007/ |access-date=September 25, 2025 |work=Detroit Free Press}}</ref>

On July 6, Skubal was named to the [[2025 Major League Baseball All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] roster, his second consecutive All-Star selection.<ref name="Romo" /> On July 12, American League (AL) manager [[Aaron Boone]] named Skubal the starting pitcher for the AL in the game.<ref>{{cite web | last=Maguire | first=Brent | title=Tarik Skubal, Paul Skenes to start 2025 MLB All-Star Game | website=MLB.com | date=2025-07-14 | url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-paul-skenes-2025-all-star-game-starters | access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref> He gave up hits to the first three batters in the game, allowing two runs in one inning as the AL lost.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 All-Star Game Box Score, July 15 |url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/allstar/2025-allstar-game.shtml |access-date=2025-10-04 |website=Baseball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

With ten strikeouts on August 19 against the [[Houston Astros]], Skubal became the first MLB pitcher to reach 200 strikeouts in 2025, the second season in a row he has done that.<ref>{{cite news |title=Skubal becomes 1st to 200 K's in '25, strengthening AL CY case |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-records-200th-strikeout-of-2025?game_pk=776685 |last=Beck |first=Jason |website=MLB.com |date=August 20, 2025 |access-date=August 20, 2025}}</ref>

For the 2025 season, Skubal went 13–6 with 241 strikeouts and an AL-leading 2.21 ERA. He also led the league's pitchers in WAR (6.6, according to [[Baseball Reference]]), ERA+ (187), and FIP (2.45), while leading the majors in WHIP (0.891), [[Bases on balls per nine innings pitched|walks per 9 innings]] (1.5), and [[strikeout-to-walk ratio]] (7.30).<ref name=br/>

His 2025 regular season efforts resulted in him winning his second consecutive AL Cy Young award.  He was the first pitcher to win consecutive awards since [[Jacob deGrom]] won the [[NL Cy Young]] in 2018 and 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schoenfield |first1=David |title=Tigers' Tarik Skubal, Pirates' Paul Skenes win Cy Young Awards |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/46947108/tigers-tarik-skubal-repeats-al-cy-young-award-winner |access-date=March 8, 2026 |publisher=ESPN.com |date=November 12, 2025}}</ref> He was the first in the American League since [[Pedro Martinez]] won the award in 1999 and 2000.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woodbery |first1=Evan |title=Tigers ace Tarik Skubal joins elite company with second Cy Young in a row |url=https://www.mlive.com/tigers/2025/11/tigers-ace-tarik-skubal-joins-elite-company-with-second-cy-young-in-a-row.html |website=mlive |access-date=13 November 2025 |language=en |date=13 November 2025}}</ref> He also became the 12th pitcher to win back-to-back Cy Young Awards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tarik Skubal is the 12th pitcher to win back-to-back Cy Young Awards! (Joins list of LEGENDARY aces) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qY8HvLY96fs |website=YouTube |date=November 12, 2025 |access-date=November 18, 2025}}</ref>

In Game 1 of the [[2025 American League Wild Card Series|AL Wild Card Series]] against the Guardians, Skubal tied a Tigers playoff record, set by [[Joe Coleman (baseball, born 1947)|Joe Coleman]] in [[1972 American League Championship Series|1972]], with 14 strikeouts. The Tigers won 2–1.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ford |first=Ryan|date=September 30, 2025 |title=Tarik Skubal stats in Game 1 of 2025 MLB playoffs vs Cleveland Guardians: How he pitched|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2025/09/30/tarik-skubal-stats-tigers-guardians-playoffs-game-1/86441812007/|access-date=September 30, 2025 |work=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> In Game 5 of the [[2025 American League Division Series|AL Division Series]] against the Mariners, Skubal broke a winner-take-all postseason record with 13 strikeouts. Earlier in the game, Skubal set a record for most strikeouts in a row in a postseason game with seven.<ref>{{cite news |last=Paul|first=Tony|date=October 10, 2025 |title=Tigers' Tarik Skubal sets MLB records in Game 5 vs. Mariners|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2025/10/10/tigers-tarik-skubal-sets-mlb-record-in-game-5-vs-mariners/86634742007/|access-date=October 10, 2025 |work=the Detroit News}}</ref> Across three games and 20.2 innings of the [[2025 Major League Baseball postseason|2025 postseason]], Skubal recorded a 1–0 record with a 1.74 ERA and 36 strikeouts.<ref name=":2" />

====2026====
On February 5, 2026, Skubal won his arbitration hearing and was awarded $32 million for the 2026 season. The Tigers had offered $19 million, forcing a three-person arbitration panel to make the decision, ultimately deciding in favor of Skubal's request. The salary decision breaks the arbitration record of $31 million awarded to [[Juan Soto]] in 2024, and is well above the former arbitration record for a pitcher, which was $19.75 million awarded to [[David Price (baseball)|David Price]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tarik Skubal wins arbitration over Tigers, to make $32M |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/47840462/sources-tarik-skubal-wins-arbitration-tigers-make-32m |last=Passan |first=Jeff |website=espn.com |access-date=9 February 2026 |language=en |date=5 February 2026}}</ref>

Skubal made his third straight Opening Day start for the Tigers on March 26 against the [[San Diego Padres]]. He earned the win with six innings of three-hit ball, striking out six, walking none and allowing one unearned run.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kevin McGonigle begins his career with 4 hits in Tigers' 8-2 win over Padres on opening day |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/recap/_/gameId/401814701 |website=espn.com |access-date=27 March 2026 |language=en |date=26 March 2026}}</ref> On May 4, it was announced Skubal would undergo surgery for loose bodies in his left elbow, a procedure that typically takes 2–3 months to recover from,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Petzold |first1=Evan |title=Tarik Skubal to undergo surgery for loose bodies in left elbow |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2026/05/04/tarik-skubal-injury-surgery-elbow-injured-list/89932684007/ |access-date=4 May 2026 |work=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> but only resulted in a six-week absence with Skubal pitching for the Tigers on June 13. On July 29, Skubal whiffed [[Taylor Ward]] of the [[Baltimore Orioles]] for his 1,000th career strikeout. By innings pitched (857), he reached the milestone faster than any Tiger in history, considerably faster than [[Max Scherzer]]'s mark of 1,000 strikeouts in {{frac|944|2|3}} innings.<ref>{{cite news |last=Beck |first=Jason |title=Skubal notches 1,000th career K in emotional final start before Deadline|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-notches-1-000th-career-strikeout |date=29 July 2026 |access-date=30 July 2026 |website=mlb.com}}</ref> By games played (153), Skubal is the second-fastest to 1,000 strikeouts by a left-hander in MLB history, behind only [[Randy Johnson]] (152 games).<ref>{{cite news |title=Tigers fans salute Tarik Skubal after 1,000th career strikeout |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/49481274/tigers-fans-salute-tarik-skubal-1000th-career-strikeout |date=29 July 2026 |access-date=30 July 2026 |website=espn.com}}</ref>

For the Tigers in 2026, Skubal went 7–5 with a 2.79 ERA, a 0.910 WHIP, and 116 strikeouts in {{frac|96|2|3}} innings.<ref name=br/>

===Los Angeles Dodgers===
On August 2, 2026, the Tigers traded Skubal to the [[Los Angeles Dodgers]] in exchange for [[Zyhir Hope]], [[River Ryan (baseball)|River Ryan]], and [[Brady Smith (baseball)|Brady Smith]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/dodgers/news/tarik-skubal-dodgers-tigers-trade|title=Dodgers deliver blockbuster, acquire Skubal from Tigers|work=mlb.com|first=Sonja|last=Chen|date=August 2, 2026|access-date=August 2, 2026}}</ref>

With the Dodgers in 2026, Skubal made 10 starts and posted a 5–2 record, with a 2.61 ERA, 1.048 WHIP and 70 strikeouts in 62 innings.<ref name=br/>

==International career==
Skubal was included on the [[United States national baseball team]] for the [[2026 World Baseball Classic]], but only played once before rejoining the Tigers for spring training since he wanted to focus on the upcoming season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Adler|first=David|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tarik-skubal-will-leave-team-usa-to-return-to-tigers-camp|title=Skubal will leave Team USA to return to Tigers camp|website=[[MLB.com]]|publisher=[[Major League Baseball]]|date=March 9, 2026|access-date=August 4, 2026}}</ref> His lone appearance came in the [[2026 World Baseball Classic Pool B|pool stage]] against [[Great Britain national baseball team|Great Britain]], allowing a home run on the opening pitch before striking out five batters on 41 pitches; the United States won 9–1.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/48138229/skubal-allows-leadoff-homer-throws-41-pitches-wbc-start|title=Skubal allows leadoff HR in 41-pitch start; Team USA wins|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=March 7, 2026|access-date=August 4, 2026}}</ref> He returned to the team to support them in the [[2026 World Baseball Classic championship|championship game]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Nightengale|first=Bob|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/mlb/wbc/2026/03/18/team-usa-wbc-venezuela-baseball-championship/89206033007/|title=USA overcome with emotion after WBC defeat: 'Loved it. But I'm still pissed.'|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=March 18, 2026|access-date=August 4, 2026}}</ref>

==Pitching style==
Skubal throws both four-seam and sinking two-seam [[fastball]]s, each averaging around {{Convert|96|mph}}, with his four-seam fastball having reached as fast as {{Convert|102.7|mph|abbr=on}}. His off-speed pitches include a [[Slider (pitch)|slider]] that averages {{Convert|88|mph|abbr=on}}, with an occasional "turbo slider" reaching as high as {{Convert|95|mph|abbr=on}}. Since 2023, his best and most used off-speed pitch is a [[changeup]] that averages {{Convert|86|mph|abbr=on}} with an elite seam-shifted wake, generating the lowest contact rate (54.6%) and highest chase rate (42.8%) of all his pitches, with a career .186 batting average against.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tarik Skubal PitchFX |url=https://www.fangraphs.com/players/tarik-skubal/22267/pitch-type-splits?position=P&data=pi&pitchtype=all |access-date=July 22, 2022 |website=[[FanGraphs]]}}</ref> Compared to most changeups, which almost always break straight downward, Skubal throws the pitch in a way that causes the seams of the baseball to catch the air in just the right way to make the ball move unpredictably. MLB.com called Skubal's changeup "the most valuable pitch in baseball," due to its league-leading +25 run value. In 2025, it was the hardest changeup to hit in the major leagues (.156 batting average against), and had the second highest whiff rate (47.0%).<ref>{{cite web |title=The best pitches we'll see this October |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/best-pitches-mlb-postseason-2025 |last=Greenspan |first=Jared |date=September 26, 2025 |access-date=October 6, 2025 |website=mlb.com}}</ref> He also occasionally throws a [[knuckle curve]] that averages {{Convert|77|mph|abbr=on}}.

2021–present | awards = [[Chicago Reader|Best Chicago Pop Artist]] | website = {{URL|https://emilybluemusic.com}} | module = {{Infobox musical artist | embed = yes | genre = {{hlist|[[Electropop]]|[[glitch pop]]|[[synth-pop]]{{cite web |last1=Nelson |first1=JR |title=Tara Terra front woman Emily Blue drops a newly expanded solo synth-pop EP |url=https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/emily-blue-tara-terra-marian-runk-whpk-blacker-face/Content?oid=69244291 |website=Chicago Reader |date=March 27, 2019 |accessdate=November 5, 2019 |archive-date=May 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200508021321/https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/emily-blue-tara-terra-marian-runk-whpk-blacker-face/Content?oid=69244291 |url-status=dead }}|[[indie pop]]{{cite web |last1=Mosk |first1=Mitch |title=Tara Terra return with irresistibly raw "Ithaca" |url=http://atwoodmagazine.com/ithaca-tara-terra-song-premiere/ |website=Atwood Magazine |date=April 2019 |accessdate=November 5, 2019}}|[[hair metal]]|[[death metal]]}} | instrument = {{hlist|Vocals|piano|guitar|synthesizer}} | label = [[Audiotree]] | associated_acts = {{hlist|Tara Terra|[[Bad City|Max Perenchio]]|[[K.Flay]]|uuskhy|Moon Mouth}} }} }} '''Emily Blue''', born '''Emily Caroline Otnes''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ɑː|t|n|ə|s}}) (born June 28 1994), is an American singer-songwriter. She{{efn|Blue uses both ''[[she/her]]'' and ''[[they/them]]'' pronouns. This article uses ''she/her'' for consistency.}} has a solo career and is the lead singer of [[Champaign]]-based [[indie rock]] band Tara Terra. Born and raised in [[Urbana, Illinois]], she now lives in Chicago and Nashville. Blue's career is characterized by sharp changes in musical style, and [[Emily Blue discography|her releases]] fall into different genre classifications, ranging from [[synth-pop]] to [[Avant-garde music|avant-garde]] and [[death metal]]. == Life and career == Emily Blue was born as Emily Caroline Otnes on June 28, 1994, in [[Urbana, Illinois|Urbana]], Illinois. She wrote her first song when she was 13, and got motivated to become a songwriter. She says her mother was the guiding figure in her home, and that she inspired her by taking a powerful female role in the household.{{cite web |last1=Rud |first1=Nico |title=Who is Emily Blue? |url=https://chicagocreatives.co/2017/05/25/who-is-emily-blue/ |website=Chicago Creatives |date=May 25, 2017 |accessdate=November 5, 2019}} She met Colin Althaus and Joey Buttlar in the early 2010s and they joined Nick Soria and Céline Broussard to form Emily Otnes and the Weekdays, later renamed to Tara Terra. Otnes changed her name to Emily Blue. Tara Terra released their debut album, ''Daughter'', in 2014. === 2016–2017: Solo career and ''Where's Your Light?'' === Blue's first single, "No Pain", was released on August 6, 2016, with lyrics about rape culture. The ''Another Angry Woman'' EP, was released on November 4, 2016, with five music tracks and three one minute interview tracks.{{cite web |last1=Corrall |first1=Cody |title=INTERVIEW: Emily Blue |url=http://www.hooliganmagazine.com/blog/2017/6/11/interview-emily-blue |website=Hooligan Mag |accessdate=November 5, 2019 |archive-date=November 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106001306/http://www.hooliganmagazine.com/blog/2017/6/11/interview-emily-blue |url-status=dead }} Its lyrics are on subjects considered taboo, but conveyed with a mellow [[indie pop]] sound. According to Blue, the title of the EP "is a title that intends to take a critical stance on our culture's lack of empathy towards survivors".{{cite web |last1=Casey |first1=Skorski |title=Another Angry Woman: An interview with Emily Blue |url=http://www.smilepolitely.com/music/another_angry_woman_an_interview_with_emily_blue/ |website=Smile Politely |date=November 4, 2016 |accessdate=November 5, 2019}} All the income from the album sales and merchandise for Another Angry Woman went to RACES (Rape Advocacy, Counseling, & Education Services) organization. Blue released the two-sided single, "Blackberries // Rico Acid" on April 7, 2017, with an up-tempo pop sound. "Blackberries" became popular on music streaming service Spotify.{{Citation needed|date=January 2023}} It was Blue's first collaboration with Max Perenchio. Tara Terra released the ''Where's Your Light?'' album in 2017, preceded by the single "Like the Clothes". Huffington Post praised the track, labeling it as the band "[showing] off their rhythmic chemistry underneath Blue's falsettos and [Colin] Althaus's bright guitar riffs." It was described as having a harder sound than their 2014 release and received mostly positive reviews.{{cite web |last1=Fountain |first1=Rasheena |title=Indie Rock Band Tara Terra Asks, Where's Your Light? |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/album-premiere-indie-rock-band-tara-terra-asks-wheres_b_592e06ace4b075342b52c12f |website=Huffington Post |date=May 30, 2017 |accessdate=November 5, 2019}} The band went on indefinite hiatus the same year. === 2018: ''*69 EP'' === {{Main|*69 (album)}} On April 6, 2018, Blue released "Cellophane", an [[Experimental music|experimental]] and [[Synthwave|heavily synthesized]] pop track. This became the first single from ''[[*69 (album)|*69]] EP'', produced by and written with [[Bad City]]'s Max Perenchio. It was released on August 8, 2018. The second song from this extended play, "Microscope", was released five days before the EP was out. The sound on the EP was described by ''Chicago Reader'' as "a glossy, idea-packed EP whose five tunes burst with pulsing [[Electronic Dance Music|electro]] beats and walloping [[synth-pop]] choruses". It was also said that a few listens to Blue's "Microscope" and "Falling in Love", "make it clear that she can translate her razor-sharp hooks into any musical language". On the album's re-release, three songs were added to the tracklist. === 2019: Tara Terra reformation and ''ICONIC'' === On January 10, 2019, Blue commercially released ''Emily Blue on Audiotree Live'' with the songs from ''*69'', except "Dum Blonde", and three of her earlier singles. On March 8 of the same year, Blue released a [[pop-rock]] cover of [[Blondie (band)|Blondie]]'s "[[Call Me (Blondie song)|Call Me]]", just three weeks before the release of Tara Terra's comeback single "Ithaca", which was revealed on April 1, 2019, premiering on Atwood Magazine. This album added Evan Opitz as official guitarist of Tara Terra. On April 7, 2019. Blue released a five-track extended play: ''Couch Surfer, Lover''. The single "Bad Decisions" was made available on all platforms on June 28, 2019, Blue's 25th birthday.{{cite web |last1=Mosk |first1=Mitch |title=Emily Blue embraces imperfections in "Bad Decisions" |url=http://atwoodmagazine.com/ebbd-bad-decisions-emily-blue/ |website=Atwood Magazine |date=July 10, 2019 |accessdate=November 5, 2019}} The cover art for the album depicted the singer [[mooning]] the camera in front of a [[McDonald's]]. On October 11, 2019, the singer released an indie-metal fusion track titled "17" on Spotify. The song was described both by reviewers and fans and by Blue herself as inspired by [[Lana Del Rey]]. On October 14, 2019, Blue announced an 18+ LGBT music festival organised by her, titled ''ICONIC''. The festival took place on December 6, at Schuba's Tavern and included performances from Chicago band Flora, artists Carlile, [[SuperKnova]], Thair and GirlBoifriend.{{cite web |last1=Blue |first1=Emily |title=ICONIC – A Queer Benefit |url=https://lh-st.com/shows/12-06-2019-iconic/ |accessdate=November 5, 2019}} According to the festival's site, a portion of the proceeds went to nonprofit organization [[Brave Space Alliance]], a pro-[[trans rights]] organization. On November 8, 2019, Blue won first place in [[Chicago Reader]]'s year-end Best Pop Artist award. === 2020-present: COVID-19, new beginnings, ''The Afterlove'' === In 2020, in light of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Blue launched an initiative entitled "Artists for Global Giving". The concept of the project was that artists in lockdown make tracks from quarantine within 24 hours, with all tracks compiled into a mixtape, the proceeds of which go to [[COVID-19]] relief funds. Many artists promoted the concept on social media, with the process being dubbed "#1DaySongChallenge". The first volume of the project, "Artists for Global Giving | Mixtape #1" was released on March 25, 2020. "Social Distance", the fourth track on the album, is performed by Blue herself. Blue released a new single titled "Aperture" on 8 May, which was first teased on 15 April.{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Charles |title=Emily Blue "Aperture" |url=http://chicago.thedelimagazine.com/43335/emily-blue-aperture |website=thedelimagazine.com |publisher=The Deli |accessdate=7 August 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} The song was premiered with a live performance on [[WFLD|Good Day Chicago]]. [[The Deli]] called the song "ethereal" and said it was "more firmly planted in Dream Pop than Blue's previous singles", while Emma Maliborski of Chicago Haze said it "manages to send listeners to a vibrant landscape through their earbuds".{{cite web |last1=Maliborski |first1=Emma |title=Emily Blue Paints an Ambient Landscape in "Aperture" |url=https://chicagohaze.com/2020/05/21/emily-blue-paints-an-ambient-landscape-in-aperture/ |website=chicagohaze.com |date=May 21, 2020 |publisher=Chicago Haze |accessdate=7 August 2020}} On 7 August 2020, following a live performance for [[Jack Daniel's]] via [[Audiotree]], with two previously unreleased tracks "Prophet" and "Glow", Blue released a single titled "Trump.". The song is a [[protest song]] against [[Donald Trump]] in the genre of [[death metal]]. Blue announced on Twitter on 27 August 2020 that she would soon release an EP. The expected date of the release is unknown as of now. On 9 October, she followed the news up with a cover of [[Lady Gaga]] and [[Ariana Grande]]'s [[Rain on Me (Lady Gaga and Ariana Grande song)|"Rain on Me"]], which features vocals from Chicago singer Thair. On 26 November 2020, Emily Blue's long-term songwriting partner Max Perenchio died at the age of 33 in a car crash in Southern California. Perenchio produced the vast majority of her releases up until that point. Emily Blue's first single of 2021, "7 Minutes", was released on 12 February. According to Wiwibloggs, it was sent to the song selection committee for [[Melodi Grand Prix 2021]] before being released as a single. The song is the first release from Blue's third studio album.{{cite web |last1=Vautrey |first1=Jonathan |title=New music this week: 20 songs from Alexander Rybak & Sirusho, Damir Kedžo & Tijana Bogicevic and more |url=https://wiwibloggs.com/2021/02/14/new-music-from-tina-karol-cleo-alekseev-sirusho-and-more/261476/ |website=[[Wiwibloggs]]|date=February 14, 2021 }} "7 Minutes" was featured on [[Noisey]]'s Top Tracks of February 2021.{{Cite web|title=The Songs That Made This Horrible February Bearable|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-best-new-songs-and-music-february-2021/|access-date=2021-07-30|website=Vice.com|date=February 26, 2021 |language=en}} The second single from the album, "See U in My Dreams", was initially scheduled to be released in June 2021. However, its release was postponed to July 23. '''Alistair William Johnston''' (born October 8, 1998) is a Canadian professional [[association football|football]] player who plays as a [[right-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Celtic}} club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and the [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada national team]].

Johnston began his senior career with [[Vaughan Azzurri]]. He later had spells with [[Major League Soccer]] teams [[Nashville SC]] and [[CF Montréal]] before signing for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in late 2022. He made his debut for Canada in 2021 and represented the country at the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] and [[2024 Copa América]].

==Early life==
Johnston was born in [[Vancouver]] to a Canadian father and an Irish mother from [[Poleglass]]. His family moved to [[Montreal]] when he was four, where he began playing soccer with [[Lakeshore SC]]. The family again moved to [[Aurora, Ontario]] when he was seven.<ref>{{Canada Soccer player|id=3772|accessdate=May 3, 2026}}</ref> There, he played youth soccer with [[Aurora FC (Canada)|Aurora FC]] and [[Richmond Hill SC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yorkregion.com/news-story/10504794-aurora-s-alistair-johnston-has-canada-s-back-on-fifa-world-cup-qualifying-trail/|title=Aurora's Alistair Johnston has Canada's back on FIFA World Cup qualifying trail|first=John|last=Cudmore|work=Aurora Banner|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

He made his debut in the Canadian youth program at an under-18 camp in 2015, when he was 16.<ref name="heads">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/soccer/2020/11/19/canadian-fullback-alistair-johnston-turning-heads-with-expansion-nashville-sc.html|title=Canadian fullback Alistair Johnston turning heads with expansion Nashville SC|first=Neil|last=Davidson|date=November 19, 2020|work=[[Toronto Star]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He played youth soccer with [[ANB Futbol]], and earned a tryout with French club [[Troyes AC]] while there.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.anbfutbol.com/news_and_buzz_june_30-2_2014.htm|publisher=[[ANB Futbol]]|title=Player Success|date=June 30, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://socceracademyalliancecanada.wordpress.com/tag/anb-futbol/page/2/|title=Seven ANB players travel to Europe|date=April 22, 2016|publisher=Soccer Academy Alliance Canada}}</ref> In 2015, he joined [[Vaughan SC]], helping them win the 2015 U-18/U-19 Disney Soccer Showcase, the 2015 OYSL U-18 League title,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://redstormsports.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/alistair-johnston/1223|title=Alistair Johnson profile|publisher=[[St. John's Red Storm men's soccer|St. John's Red Storm]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> and the 2016 and 2017 U21 [[Ontario Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ontariosoccer.net/news_article/show/816045|title=Vaughan SC Win Fourth U-21 Men's Ontario Cup in a Row|date=July 23, 2017|publisher=[[Ontario Soccer Association]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Johnston attended [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's University]] for two years, before moving to [[Wake Forest University]] in 2018 in search of a bigger challenge both in soccer and academically. He switched positions from central midfield to right-back upon joining Wake Forest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/sports/article/canadian-alistair-johnston-looks-to-take-next-soccer-step-in-mls-superdraft/|title=Canadian Alistair Johnston looks to take next soccer step in MLS SuperDraft|first=Neil|last=Davidson|date=January 9, 2020|publisher=[[CTV News]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
{{unreferenced section|date=June 2026}}
While in college, Johnston returned to Canada to play with [[League1 Ontario]] side [[Vaughan Azzurri]] from 2015 to 2019 during the college offseason. He played in the [[2019 Canadian Championship]] for Vaughan Azzurri and was sent off in the second leg of the away goals defeat to the [[HFX Wanderers FC|HFX Wanderers]].

===Nashville SC===
On January 9, 2020, Johnston was selected 11th overall by [[Nashville SC]] in the [[2020 MLS SuperDraft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/mls/mls-draft-ryan-raposo-selected-vancouver-whitecaps-1.5421252 |title=Crop of Canadians taken early in MLS draft |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |date=January 9, 2020|first=Neil|last=Davidson|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He officially signed with the club on February 25, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nashvillesc.com/post/2020/02/25/nashville-sc-extends-offers-2020-mls-superdraft-selections |title=Nashville SC Extends Offers to 2020 MLS SuperDraft Selections |date=February 25, 2020|access-date=May 3, 2026|website=Nashville SC}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], which included Nashville withdrawing from the [[MLS is Back Tournament]] due to an outbreak amongst the team,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://torontoobserver.ca/2020/06/03/aurora-soccer-player-johnston-focuses-on-positive-mental-state-during-pandemic/|title=Aurora soccer player Johnston focuses on positive mental state during pandemic|first=Keegan|last=Lavigne|date=June 3, 2020|work=The Toronto Observer|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> his debut was delayed until August 12 against [[FC Dallas]], coming on as a substitute.<ref name=heads /> He made his first start four days later, also against Dallas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/08/17/nashville-sc-youngster-alistair-johnston-hailed-coach-gary-smith-after-impressive|title=Nashville SC youngster Alistair Johnston hailed by coach Gary Smith after impressive first MLS start|date=August 17, 2020|first=Jason|last=Le Miere|publisher=[[Major League Soccer]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He helped the club reach the [[MLS Cup Playoffs|MLS Playoffs]] in their debut season, making 18 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fox17.com/sports/scoreboard/one-on-one-with-nashville-scs-alistair-johnston-on-2020-season-and-a-look-at-playoffs|title=One-on-one with Nashville SC's Alistair Johnston on 2020 season and a look at playoffs|first=Tatum|last=Everett|date=November 16, 2020|publisher=[[WZTV|WZTV Nashville - Fox 17]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

On September 22, 2021, Johnston scored his first MLS goal in a 5–1 victory over [[Inter Miami]].<ref>{{Cite web|title= Recap: Inter Miami CF 1, Nashville SC 5|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/recap-inter-miami-cf-1-nashville-sc-5|publisher=[[Major League Soccer]]|accessdate=September 22, 2021}}</ref> In December 2021, Nashville announced they were exercising Johnston's contract option, keeping him at the club through the [[2022 Major League Soccer season|2022 MLS season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nashvillesc.com/news/nashville-soccer-club-announces-2021-roster-decisions|title=Nashville Soccer Club Announces 2021 Roster Decisions|date=December 10, 2021|publisher=[[Nashville SC]]}}</ref>

===CF Montréal===
On December 23, 2021, [[CF Montréal]] acquired Johnston from Nashville in exchange for $1 million in allocation money, with Nashville also retaining a percentage of a transfer fee in a future sale.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/alistair-johnston-cf-montreal-nashville-sc-canada-canmnt-1.1738401|title=CF Montreal acquires CanMNT's Johnston|publisher=[[The Sports Network|TSN]]|date=December 23, 2021}}</ref> Montreal confirmed the deal on December 27 and announced Johnston had also signed a new contract taking him through 2023, with options for 2024 and 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/cf-montreal-acquires-canadian-international-alistair-johnston|date=December 27, 2021|title=CF Montréal acquires Canadian international Alistair Johnston|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref>

He made his debut for Montreal on February 23, as a substitute against [[Liga MX]] side [[Santos Laguna]] in the club's second leg of their [[2022 CONCACAF Champions League]] tie.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/live-at-8pm-montreal-v-santos-laguna|title=CF Montréal 3–0 Santos Laguna|date=February 23, 2022|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref> Johnston scored his first goal for Montreal on May 14, the second goal in a 2–0 victory against [[Charlotte FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/live-at-7pm-charlotte-fc-v-cf-montreal|title=Charlotte FC 0–2 CF Montréal|date=May 14, 2022|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref>

===Celtic===
[[File:Alistair Johnston, Rangers v Celtic 2 January 2023.jpg|thumb|upright=0.55|Johnston with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2023]]

In December 2022, CF Montréal announced they had transferred Johnston to [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], taking effect January 1, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.cfmontreal.com/news/alistair-johnston-transferred-to-celtic-fc|title=Alistair Johnston transferred to Celtic FC|date=December 3, 2023|publisher=[[CF Montréal]]}}</ref> He signed a 5-year contract with the [[Glasgow]] club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2022/december/03/celtic-delighted-to-sign-canadian-internationalist-alistair-johnston-on-five-year-deal/|title=Celtic delighted to sign Canadian internationalist Alistair Johnston on five-year deal|date=December 3, 2022|publisher=[[Celtic F.C.]]}}</ref> Upon the announcement, Johnston stated at a press conference that former Celtic and current CF Montréal midfielder [[Victor Wanyama]] was a major influence on his decision to move to ''the Bhoys.''<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Agent Victor Wanyama: Celtic FC transfer easy sell for Alistair Johnston |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/agent-victor-wanyama-celtic-fc-transfer-easy-sell-for-alistair-johnston |access-date=January 8, 2023 |website=MLSSoccer.com |publisher=[[Major League Soccer]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=Alistair Johnston reveals Wanyama Celtic advice | date=December 13, 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zc2FgIxvmp0 |language=en |access-date=January 8, 2023}}</ref>

Johnston made his debut for Celtic on January 2, starting against [[Old Firm|rivals]] [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and playing the entire match in a 2–2 away draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2023/january/02/kyogo-strikes-late-at-ibrox-as-honours-even-in-glasgow-derby-/|title=Kyogo strikes late at Ibrox as honours even in Glasgow derby|first=Ryan|last=Maher|date=January 2, 2023|publisher=[[Celtic F.C.]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He then made his home debut a few days later, starting again in a 2–0 win against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scots Prem (Sky Sports) |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/celtic-vs-kilmarnock/teams/465140 |access-date=January 8, 2023 |publisher=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

On March 5, 2023, Johnston scored his first goal for Celtic in a 5–1 away win against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 5, 2023 |title=St Mirren 1-5 Celtic: Ruthless Scottish Premiership leaders restore nine-point lead |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64775002 |access-date=May 3, 2026 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Johnston ended his first season at [[Celtic Park]] having helped them to a domestic treble, winning the [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership|Premiership]], the [[2023 Scottish League Cup final (February)|League Cup]] and the [[2023 Scottish Cup final|Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://vidya-ayurveda.org/ |title=jalalive |date=December 13, 2022 |last=Kaan |first=Ayhan |access-date=May 3, 2026 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Celtic |date=June 3, 2023 |title=Eightsome Reel… Celtic make history with another Treble triumph |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2023/june/03/eightsome-reel--celtic-make-history-with-another-treble-triumph/ |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref> On November 22, 2024, Johnston signed a new five-year contract with Celtic, keeping him at the club until 2029.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Celtic |date=November 22, 2024 |title=Alistair Johnston signs new Celtic contract |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2024/november/22/alistair-johnston-signs-new-celtic-contract/ |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Celtic FC |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Alistair Johnston Canada v Qatar 18 June 2026-149.jpg|thumb|271x271px|Johnston with [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]]]
Johnston accepted an invitation to the [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada national team]] camp in January 2021.<ref name="can2021">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/canada-soccer-ayo-akinola-national-team-camp-1.5853734|title=TFC's Ayo Akinola accepts invite to Canada national team camp|date=December 23, 2020|first=Neil|last=Davidson|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> He made his debut for Canada on March 25, 2021, as a 69th-minute substitute against [[Bermuda national football team|Bermuda]] in the first round of [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONCACAF)|2022 FIFA World Cup qualifying]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/canada-honduras-world-cup-qualifying-soccer-1.5964733|title=Larin, Davies team up to help Canada crush Bermuda in World Cup qualifier|accessdate=March 25, 2021}}</ref> He scored his first goal for his country in the following match, an 11–0 win against the [[Cayman Islands national football team|Cayman Islands]], which became the largest victory in the team's history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/canada-world-cup-cayman-islands/|first=John|last=Jacques|title=Canada Coasts Past Cayman Islands In Historic Eleven-Goal Win|date=March 29, 2021|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

In June 2021, Johnston was named to the 60-man preliminary squad for the [[2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/canada-names-60-man-preliminary-roster-for-next-month-s-gold-cup-1.1656962 |date=June 18, 2021 |title=Davies, David highlight Canada's preliminary roster for Gold Cup}}</ref> and on July 1 he was named to the final squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.canadasoccer.com/news/canada-soccer-announces-2021-concacaf-gold-cup-roster/ |title=Canada Soccer Announces 2021 Gold Cup Roster |date=July 1, 2021 |publisher=[[Canadian Soccer Association]]}}</ref>

In November 2022, Johnston was called up to Canada's squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canada-announces-26-man-squad-for-2022-fifa-world-cup-in-qatar|date=November 13, 2022|title=Canada announces 26-man squad for 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar|publisher=[[Canadian Premier League]]|first=Charlie|last=O'Connor-Clarke|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> where he played in all three of Canada's matches. In June 2023, he was named to Canada's 23-man squad for the [[2023 CONCACAF Nations League Finals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Former CPLers Loturi, Zator called up by Canada for 2023 Concacaf Nations League Finals|date=June 7, 2023|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canada-canmnt-2023-concacaf-nations-league-final-roster|first=Mitchell|last=Tierney|publisher=[[Canadian Premier League]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

In June 2024, Johnston was named in Canada's squad for the [[2024 Copa América]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canadasoccer.com/news/canmnt-announce-2024-copa-america-roster/|title=CANMNT ANNOUNCE 2024 COPA AMÉRICA ROSTER|date=June 15, 2024|publisher=[[Canadian Soccer Association]]}}</ref> Following the conclusion of the competition, he was named in the Team of the Tournament, being the only non-South American player included.<ref name="tott">{{Cite web|url=https://copaamerica.com/en/news/best-xi-team-tournament-copa-america-2024|title=The CONMEBOL Copa América 2024™ Best XI|website=copaamerica.com|date=July 31, 2024}}</ref> In July 2025, Johnston was called up to Canada's squad for the [[2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.onesoccer.ca/a/canmnt-announce-2025-conacaf-gold-cup-squad-roster-canada-soccer|date=July 5, 2025|title=CanMNT name full-strength squad for 2025 Concacaf Gold Cup|first=Mitchell|last=Tierney}}</ref>

In May 2026, Johnston was named to Canada's 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/world-cup-2026-canada-squad/|first=John|last=Jacques|date=May 29, 2026|title=Here’s The Canada World Cup Roster|work=Northern Tribune}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Johnston's younger brother, [[Malcolm Johnston (soccer)|Malcolm]], is also a football player and was selected in the first round of the [[2023 MLS SuperDraft]] by [[New York City F.C.|New York City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://celtsarehere.com/proud-older-brother-moment-celtic-stars-brother-drafted-by-mls-club/|title= 'Proud Older Brother Moment' – Celtic Star's Brother Drafted by MLS Club|website=Celtsarehere.com|date=December 22, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/alistair-johnston-malcolm-mls-super-draft-canada-soccer-1.6693147|title=Canada's Malcolm Johnston looks to follow brother Alistair ahead of MLS SuperDraft|website=cbc.ca|publisher=[[CBC Sports]]|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

Johnston proposed to his girlfriend in July 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/news/glasgow-news/inside-celtic-star-alistair-johnstons-29556498|title=Inside Celtic star Alistair Johnston's engagement at stunning Scots beauty spot|first=Fahad|last=Tariq|date=July 17, 2024|website=Glasgow Live|access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Callaghan |first=Joe |date=March 20, 2025 |title=Canada’s Alistair Johnston: ‘Our country is under threat, under attack’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/mar/20/alistair-johnston-canada-nations-league-celtic |access-date=May 3, 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>
