'''David Montoya Henao''' (born 1 September 1995) is a Colombian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Centre-back|Center-back]] for Chilean club [[Santiago Morning]].

==Career==
Born in [[Medellín]], Colombia, Montoya was with Escuela Belén San Bernardo, Talentos Juniors and Belén Las Playas before joining [[Itagüí Leones F.C.|Leones]], then called Deportivo Rionegro, with whom he made his professional debut.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ramírez |first1=Alfonso |title="Es un privilegio jugar en la A": David Montoya |url=https://www.elescenariodelosclasicos.com/page.php?id=3061 |website=www.elescenariodelosclasicos.com |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=es |date=4 April 2018}}</ref> With them, he won the [[2017 Categoría Primera B season#Torneo Finalización|2017 Primera B Torneo Finalización]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nieto |first1=Camilo |title=Leones cumplió el objetivo: campeón del Torneo de ascenso 2017-II |url=https://www.eltiempo.com/deportes/futbol-colombiano/leones-campeon-del-torneo-de-ascenso-2017-ii-155640 |access-date=20 March 2026 |work=El Tiempo |date=26 November 2017 |language=es}}</ref> In 2019, he was loaned out to [[Cortuluá]].<ref>{{cite news |title=TORNEO ÁGUILA David Montoya Henao es nuevo jugador de Cortuluá |url=https://www.facebook.com/WHINNERSS/photos/a.2258830984255819/2760770564061856 |access-date=20 March 2026 |publisher=WC Fút |date=23 January 2019 |language=es}}</ref><ref name="as"/>

In January 2020, Montoya moved abroad and joined on loan to [[Deportes La Serena]] in the [[Chilean Primera División]].<ref name="as">{{cite news |title=La Serena anunció tres fichajes para su desafío en Primera |url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2020/01/28/futbol/1580213255_995464.html |access-date=20 March 2026 |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=28 January 2020 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Montoya será baja en el Granate por lo que queda de torneo |url=https://www.miradiols.cl/2020/09/08/montoya-sera-baja-en-el-granate-por-lo-que-queda-de-torneo/ |access-date=20 March 2026 |work=Mi Radio LS |date=8 September 2020 |language=es}}</ref> In February 2021, he left Deportes La Serena and returned to Leones.<ref>{{cite news |title=Corte de La Serena ordena a club de fútbol profesional pagar prestaciones laborales adeudadas a jugador |url=https://www.pjud.cl/prensa-y-comunicaciones/noticias-del-poder-judicial/74597 |access-date=20 March 2026 |work=www.pjud.cl |date=3 June 2022 |language=es |quote=pasaje de vuelta a Colombia, al jugador profesional David Montoya Henao, quien terminó contrato con el club en febrero pasado.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramírez |first1=Daniel |title=Justicia le dio la razón al Sifup y ordenó a Deportes La Serena a pagar la deuda que le debe al jugador David Montoya |url=https://www.adnradio.cl/nacional-futbol/2022/02/04/david-montoya-gano-justicia-ordeno-a-la-serena-pagar-deuda-al-jugador.html |access-date=20 March 2026 |work=[[ADN Radio Chile|ADN Radio]] |date=4 February 2022 |language=es}}</ref>

During the 2024–25 season, Montoya played for Spanish club {{ill|Atlético Cortegana|es|Club Atlético Cortegana|vertical-align=sup}} in the [[Divisiones Regionales de Fútbol in Andalusia|Primera Andaluza]].<ref>{{cite web |title=David Montoya - Ex-Atlético Cortegana |url=https://www.lapreferente.com/J567588C22608/atletico-cortegana/david-montoya.html |website=www.lapreferente.com |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

In 2025, Montoya returned to Chile and joined [[Santiago City FC|Santiago City]] in the [[Segunda División Profesional de Chile|Segunda División Profesional]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Santiago City - Campeonato Segunda Division 2025 |url=http://www.solofutbol.cl/futbol%20chileno/Campeonatos%20Nacionales/equipos/Santiago%20City/Santiago%20City%202025%202%20division.htm |website=www.solofutbol.cl |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Arévalo |first1=Benjamín |title=Santiago City renueva piezas y perfila plantel para Segunda División |url=https://pasiondehincha.cl/santiago-city-renueva-piezas-y-perfila-plantel-para-segunda-division/ |access-date=20 March 2026 |work=Pasión de Hincha |date=29 January 2026 |language=es |quote=central colombiano David Montoya (29)... Montoya suma cupo extranjero para la zaga central.}}</ref> On 17 March 2026, he switched to [[Santiago Morning]].<ref>{{cite instagram |user=stgomorning |postid=DWAjJq5jT64 |title=Seguimos agrandando la banda de los bohemios. 👋 Le damos la bienvenida a David Montoya |date=17 March 2026 |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

'''Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet''' ({{IPA|fr|ʃaʁ.lin buʁ.ʒwa ta.kɛ}}; born 1986)<ref name="Durand-2022">{{cite web |last=Durand |first=Stéphane |title=Charente-Maritime: Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet fait tourner des grands noms du cinéma |url=https://www.sudouest.fr/charente-maritime/royan/charente-maritime-charline-bourgeois-tacquet-fait-tourner-des-grands-noms-du-cinema-12641044.php |url-access=subscription |website=[[Sud Ouest (newspaper)|Sud Ouest]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |language=fr |date=22 October 2022}}</ref> is a French director, screenwriter, and actress.

==Early life==
Bourgeois-Tacquet was born and raised in [[Royan]];<ref name="Durand-2022" /><ref name="Ipert-2021">{{cite web |last=Ipert |first=Fiona |title=Avec Les Amours d'Anaïs, Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet nous enchante |url=https://www.journaldesfemmes.fr/loisirs/cinema/2742163-les-amours-d-anais-charline-bourgeois-tacquet/ |website={{ill|Le Journal des femmes|fr}} |access-date=9 April 2026 |language=fr |date=13 September 2021}}</ref> her mother taught English and her father was a furniture importer.<ref name="Jøhnk Christensen-2022">{{cite web |last=Jøhnk Christensen |first=Tina |title=Exploring the Force of Desire: "Anaïs in Love" |url=https://goldenglobes.com/articles/exploring-force-desire-anais-love/ |website=[[Golden Globes]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=19 May 2022}}</ref> She became interested in acting at the age of 14 after seeing [[Isabelle Huppert]] in the play ''[[Medea (play)|Medea]]'' in [[La Rochelle]].<ref name="Ipert-2021" /><ref name="Risker-2022">{{cite web |last=Risker |first=Paul |title=Director Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet on Debut Romantic Comedy 'Anaïs in Love' |url=https://www.popmatters.com/charline-bourgeois-tacquet-interview-2022 |website=[[PopMatters]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=18 August 2022}}</ref>

She attended the Lycée Cordouan in Royan and later moved to [[Paris]] to enroll in the ''[[khâgne]]'' program at the [[Lycée Fénelon, Paris|Lycée Fénelon]].<ref name="Roz-2018">{{cite web |last=Roz |first=Denise |title=«Tout le monde m'a dit que j'étais folle» |url=https://www.sudouest.fr/charente-maritime/saint-georges-de-didonne/tout-le-monde-m-a-dit-que-j-etais-folle-2940993.php |website=[[Sud Ouest (newspaper)|Sud Ouest]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |language=fr |date=8 October 2018}}</ref> She then earned a ''{{ill|licence de lettres|fr}}'' and a master's degree in literature from [[Sorbonne University]].<ref name="Jøhnk Christensen-2022" /><ref name="Duponchel-2021">{{cite web |last=Duponchel |first=Marilou |title=Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet, une cinéaste entre contrôle et folie |url=https://www.lesinrocks.com/cinema/amoureuse-de-linstant-present-402594-15-09-2021/ |website=[[Les Inrockuptibles]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |language=fr |date=15 September 2021}}</ref> After failing the ''{{ill|agrégation de lettres|fr}}'' exam to teach literature, she applied for an internship at the publishing house [[Éditions Grasset]], from where she was later offered a full-time position.<ref name="Ipert-2021" />

==Career==
Bourgeois-Tacquet began her career working as an editorial assistant at Éditions Grasset for three years.<ref name="Jøhnk Christensen-2022" /><ref name="Risker-2022" /> Through her work connections, she secured small roles in films by [[Lucas Belvaux]], [[Philippe Le Guay]], and [[Mia Hansen-Løve]]. At the age of 25, she met producer [[Philippe Carcassonne]] and sent him two screenplays, one of which became her first short film, ''Joujou''.<ref name="Roz-2018" /><ref name="Duponchel-2021" /> Her second short film, ''{{ill|Pauline asservie|lt=Pauline, Enslaved|fr}}'', was screened in the [[Critics' Week]] section of the [[2018 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Lemercier |first=Fabien |title=A very European selection for the Cannes Critics' Week |url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/351952/ |website=[[Cineuropa]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=16 April 2018}}</ref>

Principal photography on her debut feature film, ''[[Anaïs in Love]]'', took place in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lemercier |first=Fabien |title=Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet is filming Anaïs in Love |url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/390449/ |website=[[Cineuropa]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=10 August 2020}}</ref> The film was partly inspired by an affair she had with a married man,<ref name="Jøhnk Christensen-2022" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Sippell |first=Margeaux |title=Charline Bourgeois-Tacquet's Affair Inspired Her Directorial Debut, Anaïs in Love |url=https://www.moviemaker.com/anais-in-love-director-charline-bourgeois-tacquet/ |website=[[MovieMaker]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=29 April 2022}}</ref> and was screened out of competition in the Critics' Week section of the [[2021 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Lemercier |first=Fabien |title=Six European filmmakers are set to compete in Cannes' Critics' Week |url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/405635/ |website=[[Cineuropa]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=7 June 2021}}</ref> Her second feature film, ''[[A Woman's Life (2026 film)|A Woman's Life]]'', premiered in the main competition of the [[2026 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Miranda |last2=Cabrera |first2=Michaela |title=Cannes Film Festival announces arthouse-heavy line-up as Hollywood scales back |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/cannes-film-festival-announces-arthouse-heavy-line-up-hollywood-scales-back-2026-04-09/ |website=[[Reuters]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=9 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Szalai |first=Georg |title=Cannes: Ira Sachs, Pedro Almodóvar, Asghar Farhadi, Hirokazu Kore-eda Lead Arthouse-Heavy Lineup |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/cannes-2026-selection-full-list-film-festival-lineup-1236553671/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=9 April 2026 |date=9 April 2026}}</ref>

== Biography ==

=== First years and education ===
Daniela Lima was born in [[Brasília]], the capital of [[Brazil]], in 1985, the daughter of [[Civil service|civil servants]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 4, 2025 |title=Quem é Daniela Lima, jornalista demitida da GloboNews |url=https://ndmais.com.br/comportamento/quem-e-daniela-lima-jornalista-demitida-globonews/ |url-status=live |archive-date=April 25, 2026 |access-date=April 25, 2026 |website=ND Mais |language=pt-BR|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260425161205/https://ndmais.com.br/comportamento/quem-e-daniela-lima-jornalista-demitida-globonews/}}</ref><ref name="Universo Online-2025"/><ref name="Bernardi-2026">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HTc4z6Tg7N4 |title=Eleições 2026: Vaga de vice de Haddad está aberta e pode fechar equação {{!}} Daniela Lima |date=April 23, 2026 |last=Bernardi |first=Tati |author-link=Tati Bernardi |type=Video |language=pt-br |publisher=[[Universo Online]] |access-date=2026-04-25 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> In the city, she graduated in [[Journalism]] from the [[Centro Universitário de Brasília]] (UniCeub) and began her career in 2003, whilst still at university, as an intern at ''[[Veja (magazine)|Veja]]'' magazine.<ref name="Nova-2025">{{Cite web |last=Nova |first=Daniel |date=August 4, 2025 |title=Quem é Daniela Lima, jornalista demitida da GloboNews? '''Enrique Riquelme''' (born 9 January 1989) is a Spanish businessman. He is the founder of COX Energy, a company in the renewable energy field. In 2026, he announced his candidacy for the [[2026 Real Madrid CF presidential election|Real Madrid Presidential Elections]] against current president [[Florentino Pérez]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cortegana |first=Mario |last2=Rai |first2=Guillermo |date=26 May 2026 |title=Enrique Riquelme interview on his Real Madrid: 'A new manager, and two signings already agreed' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7309112/2026/05/26/real-madrid-election-enrique-riquelme-interview/ |access-date=30 May 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=27 May 2026 |title=Real Madrid: Enrique Riquelme outlines plans as he launches presidential campaign |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c2d2y58xlg9o |access-date=30 May 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He was born in [[Cox, Spain|Cox, Alicante]].

== Real Madrid presidential candidacy ==
Riquelme announced his candidacy to run for [[List of Real Madrid CF presidents|President of Real Madrid]] on 21 May 2026<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barlow |first=Ruairidh |date=2026-05-21 |title=Real Madrid elections on: Florentino Perez rival to run |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2026/05/21/real-madrid-elections-on-florentino-perez-rival-informs-board-of-candidacy |access-date=2026-06-04 |website=Football España |language=en}}</ref> following current president Florentino Pérez's call for new board of directors elections. This was following a [[2025–26 Real Madrid CF season|trophy-less season]] which saw the departure of manager [[Xabi Alonso]] midway through January and the appointment of [[Real Madrid Castilla]] manager [[Álvaro Arbeloa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Daily |first=The Chosun |date=2026-05-25 |title=Real Madrid Concludes Troubled Season Without Trophies |url=https://www.chosun.com/english/sports-en/2026/05/25/KKZ3LYJBMZDK3I3NESF2L2PERM/ |access-date=2026-06-04 |website=The Chosun Daily |language=en}}</ref> This was the first contested [[2026 Real Madrid CF presidential election|Real Madrid presidential election]] since 2006 with incumbent president Pérez being unopposed in the last five electoral cycles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leveridge |first=Sam |title=The Ultimate Guide To Real Madrid’s 2026 Presidential Election |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/samleveridge/2026/05/31/the-ultimate-guide-to-real-madrids-2026-presidential-election/ |access-date=2026-06-04 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Real Madrid to hold 1st presidential election in 20 years |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48857225/real-madrid-presidential-election-florentino-perez-enrique-riquelme |access-date=2026-06-04 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref>

During a television appearance on 3 June, Riquelme presented a Real Madrid jersey which bore the last name of [[Erling Haaland]] on the back with Riquelme claiming that the Norwegian striker would join the club if he were elected president.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-04 |title=Erling Haaland: Man City threaten legal action over Real Madrid candidate's transfer claim |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c3r2g5zgl0vo |access-date=2026-06-04 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Riquelme further claimed that Haaland expressed desire to play for Real Madrid and had a [[Buyout clause|release clause]] available despite his current contract tying him with [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] through 2034.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ornstein |first=David |date=2025-01-22 |title=Erling Haaland signs new nine-and-a-half-year Manchester City contract |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6066077/2025/01/17/erling-haaland-man-city-contract-new/ |access-date=2026-06-04 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Both Haaland's father [[Alf-Inge Haaland|Alfie]] and his agent [[Rafaela Pimenta]] have denied the claims alongside Manchester City who expressed consideration for legal action.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jackson |first=Jamie |date=2026-06-04 |title=Manchester City threaten to sue Real Madrid presidential hopeful over Haaland |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/04/manchester-city-threaten-to-sue-real-madrid-presidential-candidate-erling-haaland-elliot-anderson |access-date=2026-06-04 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

'''Stefano Minerva''' (born 4 April 1986) is an Italian politician of the [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]] serving as a member of the [[Regional Council of Apulia]] since November 2025. He previously served as mayor of [[Gallipoli, Apulia|Gallipoli]] from 2016 to 2025 and as president of the [[Province of Lecce]] from 2018 to 2025.

==Career==
He was elected mayor of [[Gallipoli, Apulia|Gallipoli]] in the [[2016 Italian local elections]], defeating independent candidate Flavio Fasano in the runoff with 51.23% of the vote against 48.77%. Minerva was supported by a [[Centre-left coalition (Italy)|centre-left coalition]] including the [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]], the [[Union of the Centre (2002)|Union of the Centre]] and several civic lists.<ref>{{cite web |title=Comune di Gallipoli – Elezioni comunali 2016 |url=https://www.repubblica.it/static/speciale/2016/elezioni/comunali/gallipoli.html |publisher=[[la Repubblica]] |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

In 2018, Minerva was elected [[president of the Province of Lecce]], defeating Gianni Marra, the [[Centre-right coalition (Italy)|centre-right]] candidate, with 58.56% of the weighted vote.<ref>{{cite web |title=Provinciali, Stefano Minerva è il nuovo presidente della Provincia: a Lecce il centrodestra si spacca ancora |url=https://www.corrieresalentino.it/2018/10/provinciali-stefano-minerva-e-il-nuovo-presidente-della-provincia-lecce-il-centrodestra-si-spacca-ancora/ |publisher=Corriere Salentino |date=31 October 2018 |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref> He was re-elected president in 2022, defeating Michele Sperti, the mayor of [[Miggiano]], with 56,517 weighted votes (64%).<ref>{{cite news |title=Stefano Minerva si conferma presidente della provincia di Lecce |url=https://www.rainews.it/tgr/puglia/articoli/2022/11/pug-Stefano-Minerva-presidente-Provincia-di-lecce-a47616a9-3259-44df-8988-4f442589a3e0.html |work=[[RAI|Rai News]] |date=11 November 2022 |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Minerva riconfermato presidente della Provincia di Lecce |url=https://www.lecceprima.it/politica/minerva-riconfermato-presidente-provinca-lecce.html |work=LeccePrima |date=11 November 2022 |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref>

In the [[2025 Apulian regional election]], Minerva was elected to the [[Regional Council of Apulia]] in the Lecce constituency on the Democratic Party list, receiving 31,917 preference votes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Minerva Stefano|url=https://www.consiglio.puglia.it/minerva-stefano|publisher=Regional Council of Apulia|access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Minerva sbanca nel Pd, Pagliaro record di voti.
